The results show that high mining stress, soft rock mass, and absent floor support dominate the deformation and failure of the 1103 roadway. Enhancing roof–rib support strength mitigates floor deformation and plastic zone depth, while strengthened floor support reduces rib deformation and plastic zone depth. Stable floor and ribs further improve roof stability. A roof–rib–floor coordinated support technology is proposed by integrating roof–rib hierarchical support and grouted floor cable bundles. For the roof and ribs, short and long cables construct a hierarchical support structure with strong shallow and weak deep reinforcement to achieve mechanical coupling between supports and surrounding rock. For the floor, high-strength cable bundles combined with grouting reinforcement improve deformation resistance. The corresponding control parameters for the 1103 roadway are determined and verified by field tests. The proposed theory and technology offer references for surrounding rock control of deep roadways under high mining stress.

item.title: New Polyneolignans from Nothotsuga longibracteata Growing in China
item.description:
Abstract
Four new polyneolignans (1–4) along with two known lignans were isolated from the heartwood of Nothotsuga longibracteata. Their structures were elucidated by high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HR-ESIMS), together with spectroscopic methods including 1D/2D-NMR. Subsequent ECD computational analysis was further applied to confirm the stereochemistry of the undescribed polyneolignans. The plausible MS/MS fragmentation pathways of compounds 1 and 4 were proposed based on data acquired via electrospray ionization in negative ion mode. The summarized fragmentation rules facilitate the preliminary screening of analogous lignan constituents in botanical samples. Their cytotoxic activities against three cell lines (A172, SH-SY5Y, and HeLa) were evaluated using the 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay. Compound 2 exhibited a mild inhibitory effect against A172 cells, with an IC50 value of 25.97 μM.

item.title: Sustainable Alumina/Silk Fibroin Hybrid Dielectrics for Low-Temperature Fabrication of Flexible Organic Electronics
item.description:
Abstract
The transition toward sustainable organic electronics requires fabrication processes with reduced thermal budgets together with the integration of eco-compatible functional materials. Here, we report a sustainable hybrid dielectric platform based on low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) combined with silk fibroin (SF), a naturally derived protein, for flexible organic field-effect transistors (OFETs). An 80 °C ALD process was developed to deposit Al2O3 layers directly on flexible polyethylene naphthalate (PEN), chosen as a model mechanically compliant and thermally sensitive substrate. To engineer the dielectric/semiconductor interface, ultrathin SF layers were deposited on Al2O3 and compared with poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) as the synthetic benchmark. Morphological, dielectric, electrical and mechanical investigations show that SF forms continuous films on low-temperature ALD Al2O3 and supports a semiconductor morphology comparable to that obtained on PMMA-buffered interfaces. OFETs incorporating Al2O3/SF hybrid dielectrics operate at gate voltages below 20 V with low leakage currents and carrier mobilities of the order of 1 cm2 V–1 s–1, and retain field-effect operation at a bending radius of 5 mm. Remarkably, this is achieved with as-cast SF, whereas PMMA requires a prolonged thermal treatment. Combining low-temperature oxide processing with natural biopolymers, this platform offers a route toward sustainable, biobased and eco-compatible organic electronics.

item.title: Structure–Activity Relationship of N-(2-(Piperidin-1-yl)phenyl)benzene-1,4-disulfonamides as TRPML1 Agonists
item.description:
Abstract
Transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) is a lysosomal Ca2+ channel that regulates lysosomal trafficking, autophagy, and membrane repair. Its pharmacological activation represents a promising strategy for treating lysosomal dysfunction-related diseases, including lysosomal storage disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, muscular dystrophies, infectious diseases, and inflammatory disorders. However, existing TRPML1 agonists suffer from limitations that restrict their utility as in vivo probes and therapeutic leads. We report a comprehensive structure–activity relationship (SAR) study of N-(2-(piperidin-1-yl)phenyl)benzene-1,4-disulfonamides that delivered potent, selective, and pharmacokinetically improved TRPML1 agonists. Systematic scaffold optimization revealed key structural determinants of channel activation, yielding substantial potency gains alongside improved physicochemical, metabolic, and pharmacokinetic properties. Refinement of the aryl sulfonamide substituents and piperidine-containing moieties established clear SAR trends that enhanced cellular activity. Lead compounds exhibited robust TRPML1 agonism, high selectivity over related TRP channels, and in vivo-compatible pharmacokinetics. These studies validate this scaffold as a privileged chemotype for TRPML1 activation, providing optimized chemical probes for investigating TRPML1 biology and a foundation for therapeutic development across multiple indications.

item.title: Design of Sustainable Formulations for Nanodosing: Insight into Fatty Acid Profile Modulation in Tenebrio molitor Larvae
item.description:
Abstract
In the context of sustainable insect production,Tenebrio molitor larvae (TML) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional livestock systems. Their rich nutritional profile is characterized by high protein content and favorable lipid composition. Herein, we developed nanovectors based on exopolysaccharides derived from Neocyanospira capsulata(Es) or olive pomace (O), combined with egg yolk phospholipids (E) to deliver oils obtained from the seeds ofPerilla frutescens L. (Britt.) (Pf) andSclerocarya birrea (A.Rich.) (Sb) as a dietary supplement in TML. These oils differ significantly in their lipid composition: Pf presents high levels of C18:3 n-3, whose increase may be desirable in TML, while Sb has a considerable amount of C18:1 n-9, along with relatively higher proportions of C16:0 and C18:0. Both plain and oil-loaded nanovectors were characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and ζ-potential to obtain size distribution, shape, and surface charge. The oils were administered to TML through nanovectors at an extremely low dose of 3.15 nL per larva per day, and their effect on the fatty acid profile was investigated. Results showed that Pf-nanovectors increased C18:3 n-3 in treated larvae, whereas the free oil emulsion administered at the same dose did not produce comparable effects. All oil-loaded nanovectors altered the relative proportions of saturated fatty acids and monounsaturated fatty acids compared to the control treatments, suggesting that encapsulated lipids modulate larval lipid metabolism. All these findings support the potential of nanovectors as low-dose delivery systems for modulating the lipid composition of TML.

item.title: Activating Interlayer Organic Redox Sites in Hybrid Layered Vanadium Oxides for Li-Ion Batteries via Dopamine-Derived Carbonization
item.description:
Abstract
Chemical preintercalation of redox-active organic molecules can enhance the specific capacity of layered metal oxides by introducing interlayer redox sites alongside intralayer redox centers. However, their practical redox activity in hybrid electrodes is often limited due to sluggish charge transport kinetics. Here, we show that dopamine (DOPA) carbonization activates 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (DAAQ) molecules in bilayered vanadium oxide (BVO) hybrid electrodes, resulting in notable capacity improvement in nonaqueous Li-ion cells. BVO preintercalated solely with DAAQ (DAAQ-100) is compared with BVO preintercalated with both DAAQ and DOPA, followed by DOPA carbonization (DAAQ-65/DOPA). We found that DOPA carbonization competes with DAAQ preintercalation, reducing the interlayer DAAQ fraction while increasing hydration, yet preserving hydrogen-bond cross-linking between DAAQ and V–O layers, which enhances structural stability. Notably, DAAQ-65/DOPA exhibits a unique nanoscroll morphology, in contrast to the nanobelt morphology of DAAQ-100. Transmission electron microscopy suggests formation of interlayer carbon domains in DAAQ-65/DOPA and cyclic voltammetry indicates that DOPA-derived carbon domains activate interlayer DAAQ redox sites and enhance vanadium redox activity, which is attributed to improved charge transfer. Consequently, DAAQ-65/DOPA delivers a high initial specific capacity of ∼240 mAh g–1 at 20 mA g–1 and improved rate capability of ∼160 mAh g–1 at 200 mA g–1, outperforming DAAQ-100. Electrochemical analysis, supported by galvanostatic intermittent titration (GITT) and Nyquist plots, reveals fast charge transport kinetics arising from enhanced electron and Li+ mobility. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that DOPA carbonization can activate interlayer organic redox sites in hybrid electrodes, offering a new strategy to enhance energy storage performance.

item.title: Construction of Chloromethyl Esters from Carboxylic Acids Using Bromochloromethane and Further Transformation to Nitrate Esters
item.description:
Abstract
A method for the synthesis of chloromethyl esters from carboxylic acids and bromochloromethane was developed. The reaction, utilizing Cs2CO3 and bromochloromethane, exhibited a broad substrate scope, encompassing aromatic, aliphatic, and heteroaromatic compounds; natural products; and medicinal drugs. The system was extended to the production of nitrate esters from chloromethyl esters and silver nitrate.

item.title: 3,4-Bis(benzyloxy)benzaldehyde-Derived Hydrazones: Synthesis, α-Amylase-Selective Inhibition, Antioxidant Profiling, and In Silico Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Carbohydrate-hydrolyzing enzymes (α-amylase and α-glucosidase) are clinically validated targets for controlling postprandial hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and oxidative stress is a recognized contributor to disease progression. Herein, a series of hydrazone Schiff bases derived from 3,4-bis(benzyloxy)benzaldehyde were synthesized by acid-catalyzed condensation of the aldehyde with para-substituted phenylhydrazines and were characterized by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, FT-IR spectroscopy, and high-resolution mass spectrometry; chromatographic purity was established by RP-HPLC (94.5–98.6 area % at 350 nm). The series was evaluated for in vitro inhibition of porcine pancreatic α-amylase and yeast α-glucosidase and for antioxidant capacity using four complementary assays (DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, and CUPRAC). The compounds displayed a pronounced α-amylase preference: compound 9 (IC50 = 160.40 ± 2.05 μg/mL) and compound 7 (IC50 = 166.01 ± 2.64 μg/mL) were the most potent and exceeded acarbose under the assay conditions (IC50 = 232.66 ± 4.93 μg/mL); on a molar basis, both are essentially equipotent with the reference drug (345.2 ± 4.4 and 378.6 ± 6.0 μM versus 360.4 ± 7.6 μM), and IC50 values are reported in both units throughout (Table 1). α-Glucosidase inhibition was moderate, with the para-chloro analogue 3 being the most active (IC50 = 83.13 ± 6.53 μg/mL; 187.7 ± 14.7 μM). The selectivity index (IC50 α-glucosidase/IC50 α-amylase) spans 0.22 for 3 to 2.38 for 9, so a single para-substituent determines which carbohydrase is preferred. Antioxidant behavior was assay-dependent: compounds 1 and 4 delivered the highest ferric-reducing power (FRAP = 1854.0 ± 1.5 and 1786.7 ± 5.2 μmol Fe2+/g), and compound 5 gave the strongest CUPRAC response (280.95 ± 3.43 mg GAE/g). Molecular docking against α-amylase (PDB 1B2Y) and α-glucosidase (PDB 3TOP), together with SwissADME, QikProp, and ADMETlab profiling, provides a structural rationale for the observed substituent effects. These results define a clear, substituent-driven selectivity relationship within a lipophilic dibenzyloxy hydrazone framework and establish the DBZO-hydrazone scaffold as a tractable system for further optimization.

item.title: In Silico Identification of Peptide Pharmacophoric Determinants and Complementary Binding Hotspots on Fungal Grr1
item.description:
Abstract
The growing burden of human and plant fungal diseases, compounded by limited therapeutic options and emerging antifungal resistance, underscores the need to identify novel molecular targets for antifungal intervention. In this context, the fungal F-box protein Grr1 acts as the substrate-recognition component of the SCF ubiquitin ligase complex, binding phosphorylated degrons to direct substrate degradation and regulate key cellular processes. However, the structural and energetic determinants governing phosphodegron recognition by the Grr1 leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain remain poorly characterized. Here, we investigated the molecular basis of Grr1 recognition of phosphodegrons derived from the substrates Cln2 and Gic2 and evaluated whether phosphomimetic substitutions could preserve their interaction with the LRR domain. Structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, binding free-energy calculations, per-residue energy decomposition, and pharmacophore modeling were integrated to characterize the Grr1-degron interfaces and identify their major recognition determinants. Phosphorylation was required to maintain stable association of both degrons with the concave surface of the Grr1 LRR domain. Per-residue energy analysis revealed a conserved basic recognition surface comprising Arg418, Arg496, Lys498, Arg550, Lys608, Arg680, and Arg709, with Lys498, Arg550, Arg680, and Arg709 emerging as the principal energetic contributors shared by both complexes. Together, these residues form an electropositive environment that coordinates the degron phosphate groups, while pharmacophore mapping identified complementary molecular features associated with ligand recognition. Remarkably, substitution of the phosphorylated residues with aspartate preserved the calculated binding free energy of both degrons, whereas glutamate substitution disrupted stable binding, indicating that phosphomimetic recognition depends not merely on negative charge but critically on its precise spatial positioning within the recognition interface. Collectively, these findings define a conserved structural and energetic mechanism of phosphodegron recognition by fungal Grr1 and identify molecular features that can be exploited for ligand development. This framework supports the rational design of phosphomimetic peptides and other competitive ligands targeting the Grr1 substrate-recognition interface and provides a foundation for exploring this conserved regulatory system as a potential strategy for antifungal intervention.

item.title: Reactive-Extruded PLA/PBAT/Bentonite Nanocomposites for Diffusion-Controlled Urea Release in Sustainable Fertilizer Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Approximately 70% of conventional fertilizers applied to soil are lost to the environment, mainly through leaching, especially in sandy and organic soils. This inefficiency increases environmental impact and reduces nutrient use efficiency. Controlled-release fertilizers (CRFs) have emerged as a viable strategy to regulate nutrient availability over time. In this context, biodegradable polymers are promising coating materials due to their ability to degrade gradually in soil. Blends based on poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) have been investigated; however, their thermodynamic immiscibility compromises interfacial adhesion and overall performance. To overcome this limitation, in situ reactive extrusion was employed using maleic anhydride as a grafting agent and dicumyl peroxide as an initiator, aiming to enhance phase compatibility. Additionally, the fully organomodified bentonite clay was incorporated as a functional filler and urea adsorbent. PLA/PBAT (70/30 wt %) system containing 2 phr maleic anhydride, 1 phr dicumyl peroxide, and 3 wt % bentonite was processed under different screw speeds and feed rates to determine the optimal conditions of processing. The composites were characterized in terms of thermal behavior, morphology, and water absorption. The optimal formulation, obtained at lower screw speed and higher feed rate, exhibited improved physicochemical properties. A CRF was produced by adding 10 wt % of urea to the optimized system. Leaching tests demonstrated gradual nutrient release, with a maximum released fraction 20.7% lower than that of the PLA/PBAT/urea system without bentonite clay, confirming the positive effect of bentonite on nutrient retention and controlled-release performance.

item.title: Bioinspired Melanin Coatings Generated by Artificial Manganese Metalloenzymes for Sustainable Hair Pigmentation
item.description:
Abstract
The design of next-generation hair colorants is progressively moving toward bioinspired methodologies that reproduce natural melanogenesis under environmentally benign and mild reaction conditions. Among these approaches, catalysts displaying catecholase-mimicking behavior have attracted considerable interest as sustainable substitutes for conventional oxidative dyeing systems, owing to their capacity to induce melanin formation while reducing structural damage to hair fibers. Motivated by the multifunctional nature of melanin in living organisms, where it acts not only as a pigment but also as a UV-screening and antioxidant material; herein, we describe a chemoenzymatic strategy for the in situ deposition of synthetic melanin-like coatings on human hair through Mn-based artificial metalloenzymes. The catalytic system is based on colloidal manganese nanoparticle–enzyme hybrids engineered to exhibit oxidase-like activity. Manganese was selected due to its abundance, low toxicity, cost-effectiveness, and advantageous physicochemical characteristics. Notably, the incorporation of surfactants during hybrid preparation markedly improved both catalytic efficiency and thermal robustness, affording highly active metalloenzymatic assemblies capable of rapidly oxidizing dopamine and triggering polymerization within minutes under aqueous, base-free conditions at ambient temperature. This biomimetic process enables localized melanin generation directly on hair fibers, resulting in homogeneous, tunable, and natural-appearing coloration with excellent resistance to repeated washing and thermal exposure. In addition to cosmetic pigmentation, the deposited melanin-like layers may impart supplementary protective properties, including enhanced UV blocking and mitigation of photoinduced damage. Collectively, these findings introduce a sustainable platform for multifunctional hair dyeing and demonstrate the potential of Mn-derived artificial metalloenzymes in advanced cosmetic and surface-coating technologies.

item.title: Food Waste-to-Biochar from Low-Temperature Microwave-Assisted and Conventional Pyrolyses for Supermarket Food Waste Sustainability
item.description:
Abstract
This study investigated the physicochemical characteristics of supermarket food waste (SFW) biochar produced through low-temperature conventional pyrolysis (CP) and microwave-assisted pyrolysis (MP) to evaluate its potential for sustainability applications. Conventional pyrolysis at 300 °C (CP-SFW-300) produced biochar with high fixed carbon (FC) (48.1 wt % db), ash (11.8 wt % db), and carbon (C) (57.1 wt % db) contents, high higher heating value (HHV) (22.9 MJ/kg db), high N:C (0.1) but low H:C (0.9) ratios, and reduced abundance of oxygen-containing functional groups. In contrast, microwave-assisted pyrolysis at 240 °C (MP-SFW-240) produced biochar with high volatile matter (VM) (66.5 wt % db), abundant oxygen-containing functional groups, and more developed porosity and surface area (11.0 m2/g). These characteristics indicate that both CP-SFW-300 and MP-SFW-240 have potential as quality solid fuels and as substitutes for low-rank coals as their HHVs are comparable while offering the potential for lower greenhouse gas emissions. Furthermore, MP-SFW-240 may offer advantages for soil amendment by improving water retention and organic matter supply, although its lower ash content may reduce its contribution of mineral nutrients compared with CP-SFW-300. These findings demonstrate that low-temperature pyrolysis can tailor the characteristics of SFW biochar for specific sustainability applications while providing a sustainable pathway for SFW recovery.

item.title: Codelivery of Docetaxel and Dexamethasone from Microcapsules Based on Dimorphandra mollis Galactomannan and Syagrus coronata Oil Nanoemulsion
item.description:
Abstract
Docetaxel (DTX) is a chemotherapeutic agent widely used in the treatment of solid tumors; however, its clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic distribution, and dose-dependent toxicity. Dexamethasone (DEX) is commonly coadministered to reduce adverse effects associated with taxane-based therapies. In this study, a polysaccharide-based codelivery system was proposed to improve the controlled release and therapeutic performance of both drugs. Microcapsules were developed using the spray-drying technique, employing galactomannan extracted from Dimorphandra mollis as the polymeric matrix and incorporating an oil-in-water nanoemulsion based on Syagrus coronata oil loaded with both drugs. The systems were characterized in terms of structural morphology, thermal properties, encapsulation efficiency, in vitro cytotoxicity, and release profile. The results demonstrated the formation of amorphization within the polymeric matrix, as well as the formation of spherical microcapsules containing the drug-loaded nanoemulsion, with an average size of 2.57 ± 0.92 μm. High encapsulation efficiency was observed for DEX (96.19 ± 1.78%), whereas DTX showed moderate retention (52.15 ± 1.08%) after microencapsulation. In vitro release studies indicated a diffusion-controlled release mechanism. Cytotoxicity assays revealed that both the free drugs and the encapsulated system showed cytotoxic activity against HCT-116 colorectal carcinoma cells, whereas no cytotoxicity was observed for the encapsulated system in the L929 cell line. Overall, the system developed represents a promising strategy for the simultaneous delivery of different drugs.

item.title: Study on a Solid Retarded Acid System for Acid Fracturing in High-Temperature Carbonate Reservoirs
item.description:
Abstract
Acid fracturing is a key stimulation technology for high-temperature carbonate geothermal and hydrocarbon reservoirs. However, conventional hydrochloric acid systems suffer from rapid acid–rock reactions at high temperatures, strong corrosivity, large storage demands, and safety and environmental concerns. Here, a novel solid acid, MA-A (Modified Anhydride-based Acid), was prepared by modifying an organic acid anhydride, followed by metathesis and high-temperature calcination. FT-IR confirmed the introduction of carboxyl groups, providing the basis for sustained acid release. The acid-generation performance, dissolution behavior, acid–rock reaction kinetics, corrosion resistance, etched-fracture morphology, and fracture conductivity of MA-A were systematically evaluated. The results showed that 17% MA-A at 120 °C generated an effective acid concentration equivalent to 11.4% HCl and sustained H+ release for approximately 140 min, confirming its excellent retarded acid-generation capability. For Maokou Formation carbonate rock, 25% MA-A achieved an average dissolution rate of 90.2%, while its acid–rock reaction rate was lower than that of conventional hydrochloric acid systems. Moreover, MA-A maintained superior fracture conductivity retention under high closure stress. In addition, under the experimental conditions, MA-A caused much less corrosion of N80 steel than conventional acids, and with corrosion inhibitor GT, the system met high-temperature application requirements. Although the initial conductivity of MA-A-etched fractures was lower than that of gelled acid, it declined more slowly under high closure pressure, indicating better flow-channel retention. Overall, MA-A exhibited favorable acid-release, corrosion-control, and fracture-conductivity characteristics under the investigated laboratory conditions.

item.title: Nose-to-Brain Co-delivery of Temozolomide and Ganoderma lucidum Spore Oil in a Microemulsion for Enhanced Glioblastoma Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Temozolomide (TMZ)-based chemotherapy for glioblastoma (GBM) is severely limited by the blood–brain barrier (BBB) and the highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Ganoderma lucidum spore oil (GSO) has TME-remodeling capacity, but its efficient delivery to the brain remains challenging. Here, we developed a TMZ and GSO coloaded microemulsion (TMZ&GSO-MEs) optimized for intranasal nose-to-brain delivery. Using an “active ingredient-as-excipient” design, GSO partially replaced the conventional oil phase, resulting in a uniform nanoscale formulation (∼35 nm), high encapsulation efficiency (92.6%), and sustained release. TMZ&GSO-MEs significantly enhanced cellular uptake of both TMZ and GSO and exhibited superior antiproliferative activity in GL261 cells compared to free TMZ. In an orthotopic Luc-GL261 glioma model, intranasal administration of TMZ&GSO-MEs markedly suppressed tumor growth (inhibition rate 66.5%) and extended survival (25% of mice alive at day 60). Mechanistically, GSO reprogrammed the TME by increasing M1-type tumor-associated macrophages, CD8+ T cells, and activated dendritic cells, while decreasing M2-type macrophages and TGF-β1 and shifting serum cytokines toward a Th1-dominant profile. Notably, the formulation showed a favorable safety profile with no significant body weight loss or hepatorenal toxicity. Collectively, this nose-to-brain microemulsion integrates enhanced intracranial delivery, chemo-immunotherapeutic synergy, and reduced toxicity, offering a promising strategy for GBM therapy.

item.title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Segmentation Model for Micropores in Bituminous Coal HRTEM Images
item.description:
Abstract
Rapid and reproducible segmentation of pore-like gaps in coal high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images is valuable for quantitative microstructural analysis. We developed WT-UNet from a VGG-encoder U-Net by replacing conventional decoder-side detail convolution in all four feature-fusion stages with wavelet convolution (WTConv). The data set comprised 53 manually annotated original HRTEM images from 14 bituminous coals and 3896 retained pore regions after physical-scale harmonization. A coal-sample-level split assigned 37 images from ten coals to training, 8 images from two coals to validation, and 8 images from two other coals to independent testing. Training-only geometric and brightness transformations produced 222 training pairs. On the independent test set, WT-UNet achieved 92.73% pixel accuracy, 45.15% mean intersection over union (mIoU), 60.34% mean pixel accuracy (mPA), and 28.63% mean pore-class IoU (mIoUpore). The corresponding U-Net values were 92.58%, 44.07%, 58.96%, and 27.19%, while FCN-ResNet50 and DeepLabV3-ResNet50 achieved mIoUs of 42.88% and 43.30%. WT-UNet obtained the best aggregate performance among the four models and improved the IoU of all three pore-size categories relative to the matched U-Net. These results demonstrate that decoder-side wavelet feature processing improves multiscale pore representation and provides an efficient automatic tool for HRTEM pore-image analysis.

item.title: Study on Corrosion and Scaling Risks and Prevention/Control Measures of Water Injection Systems in Middle East Oilfields
item.description:
Abstract
To address the severe scaling and corrosion challenges in water injection systems of high-salinity and acidic oilfields in the Middle East, a combined approach of laboratory experiments, software simulation, and machine learning was employed to systematically investigate the scaling characteristics, corrosion behavior, and performance of corrosion inhibitors. CaSO4, CaCO3, and SrSO4 were identified as the dominant scale types. The effects of temperature, calcium ion concentration, CO2 partial pressure, and chloride ion concentration on scaling and corrosion were elucidated, and a high-accuracy machine-learning scale-prediction model was established. It achieves favorable prediction performance for three scale types (CaCO3, CaSO4, and SrSO4) on the test set, with coefficients of determination R2 all no less than 0.93, which enables rapid on-site scale-formation risk identification. The mechanism by which elevated calcium ion concentration aggravates localized corrosion was clarified. When the scale layer is incomplete, an increase in Ca2+ causes uneven distribution of the scale layer and the formation of microgalvanic couples, accelerating the initiation and propagation of localized corrosion. For example, the localized corrosion rate of L80 steel can reach 2.555 mm/y when the concentration of Ca2+ is 20000 mg/L. The multiscale inhibition mechanism of an imidazoline quaternary ammonium salt corrosion inhibitor was explored, and a prevention-control strategy combining water quality ion regulation and corrosion inhibitor injection was proposed. Controlling the Ca2+ content in water below 6000 mg/L and SO2–4 content below 1000 mg/L can effectively reduce the scaling risk of CaSO4. Injecting 100 ppm of No.3 corrosion inhibitor can realize both scale control and localized corrosion suppression, with a corrosion inhibition efficiency of over 94%. The research outcomes can directly guide the mitigation of scaling and corrosion in water injection systems of high-salinity and acidic oilfields in the Middle East, with expected reductions in pipeline perforation accidents and significant extensions of equipment service life.

item.title: Incorporation of Nanocellulose into Gelatin Films as Potential Film Matrices for Oral Disintegrating Film Applications with Improved Handling Stability
item.description:
Abstract
Oral disintegrating films (ODFs) require sufficient mechanical strength for handling while maintaining rapid disintegration in the oral cavity. In this study, gelatin–nanocellulose composite films were prepared using sulfated cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) and carboxymethylated cellulose nanofibers (CMCNFs) to investigate the influence of nanocellulose type and concentration on film properties. Mechanical testing demonstrated that the incorporation of nanocellulose preserved the baseline tensile strength and stiffness of gelatin films required for handling, while modifying ductility-related properties (elongation at break and toughness) primarily through a humidity-driven effect. Notably, CMCNFs retained a higher elongation at break than CNCs, preserving ductility relevant to film handling. Disintegration tests indicated that the incorporation of nanocellulose altered the disintegration behavior without hindering rapid water-triggered dissolution. These results were supported by scanning electron microscopy and polarized optical microscopy, which revealed that CNCs contributed to matrix densification, whereas CMCNFs formed fibrillar network structures at higher concentrations. Among the tested formulations, CMCNF concentrations in the range of 0.2–0.5 wt % represent a promising concentration range based on the qualitative balance observed among mechanical properties, disintegration behavior, and surface morphology, supporting these gelatin–nanocellulose composites as candidate film matrices for ODF applications.

item.title: Integrated CO 2 -EOR and Post-EOR Storage in a Mature Waterflooded UKCS Sandstone Reservoir: Recovery-Retention-Pressure Trade-offs from Compositional Simulation
item.description:
Abstract
This study evaluates miscible CO2-enhanced oil recovery, post-EOR CO2 storage, and long-term postinjection behavior in a mature offshore sandstone reservoir using compositional simulation. A PVT-tuned Peng–Robinson model gave a pure-CO2 minimum miscibility pressure of 2,528 psia by the multiple-mixing-cell method, and reservoir pressure remained above this value in all CO2-EOR cases. Five strategies (continuous CO2; fixed and tapered water-alternating-gas (WAG); a CO2 slug followed by WAG; and simultaneous water-and-gas injection) were compared from a common 2027 reference state. A 36-month CO2 slug followed by alternating six-month CO2 and six-month water periods was preferred: it produced 69.61 MMstb (8.64% of stock-tank oil initially in place), 50.06 MMstb more than continued waterflooding, and retained 9.86 of 21.42 Mt injected CO2 (46.0%). Post-EOR storage at 140 MMscf/d for 15 years, selected from three rate cases because injectivity rather than nominal rate controlled the stored mass, raised the total retained CO2 to 44.81 Mt (79.5% of 56.37 Mt injected); field-average pressure then declined from 6,955 to 6,385 psia over 100 years of shut-in monitoring. Plume expansion was limited, CO2 partitioned progressively into the oleic and aqueous phases, and mobile gas-phase CO2 decreased. The results show that a single mature, heavily waterflooded UKCS reservoir can deliver 6.2 percentage points of additional recovery and retain close to 45 Mt CO2 within its estimated operating-pressure envelope, providing a quantified reservoir-engineering basis for repurposing late-life North Sea oil fields as CO2 storage sites. Geomechanical, well-integrity, surface-processing, economic and lifecycle assessments are required before implementation.

item.title: A Methodological Framework for Dual-Energy Synchrotron XFM Characterization of Stratified Historical Glass: A Peranakan Bead Case Study
item.description:
Abstract
We present a technically focused, quantitative workflow for the depth-aware characterization of stratified historical glass using dual-energy synchrotron X-ray fluorescence microscopy (XFM). Demonstrated on a severely degraded Peranakan potash-lead–arsenic glass bead cross-section, this methodological case study establishes a reproducible template for mitigating common confounders in heritage glass analysis, such as self-absorption, matrix effects, and line overlaps. The specimen was embedded and polished to a flat internal surface, enabling coregistered optical, XRF, and scattering measurements under a fixed geometry. A paired excitation scheme was employed: a low-energy beam (7.05 keV) optimized for surface-confined, light-element sensitivity, and a high-energy beam (18.5 keV) for deeper penetration and heavy-element detection. Full XRF spectra were quantified pixel-wise using dynamic analysis (GeoPIXE) and evaluated using robust region-of-interest (ROI) statistics. The dual-energy approach yielded concrete, quantifiable improvements over single-energy methods. The 7.05 keV scan successfully isolated light-element dynamics free from heavy-element interference, revealing a massive depletion of potassium in the altered layer (mean concentration dropping from ∼3.2% to 1.84%, Hedges’ g = −7.19). Conversely, the 18.5 keV scan penetrated the bulk to quantify heavy-element leaching, demonstrating concurrent losses in arsenic (0.97% to 0.89%, g = −1.00) and lead (2.06% to 1.89%, g = −1.19). Furthermore, simultaneous scattering data at 18.5 keV provided critical structural context: a sharp decrease in elastic scattering (g = −0.70) coupled with increased Compton scattering (g = 0.10) confirmed the replacement of high-Z modifiers with a lower-density, hydrated silica gel. Correlation analysis further revealed chemical reorganization, such as a strong As–Pb colocalization (r ∼ +0.42) emerging exclusively within the altered zones. By combining complementary energies, full-spectrum fitting, and a dual-mode data presentation strategy (mapped images alongside distribution-based box/violin plots), this protocol delivers practical depth discrimination and robust quantification for both light and heavy elements. Ultimately, this work provides a transparent, statistically rigorous framework for the reliable analysis of fragile, stratified cultural heritage materials

item.title: In Situ Green Synthesis of Antibacterial Copper Nanostructures on Fabrics for Water Filtration Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Diarrheagenic Escherichia coli is a major global health concern responsible for significant mortality, particularly among young children. Copper nanostructures (Cu-NSFs) exhibit antimicrobial activity against various pathogens; however, practical and stable immobilization remains challenging. In this study, Cu-NSFs were synthesized in situ on poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) cheesecloth, offering a one-step, time-efficient alternative to conventional ex situ nanoparticle incorporation methods. Orange peel extracts and ascorbic acid were effective as both reducing and stabilizing agents, minimizing the risk of residual hazardous chemicals in treated water. The immobilized Cu-NSFs were characterized by using X-ray diffraction, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and field emission scanning electron microscopy, confirming successful deposition. Antibacterial assays demonstrated that Cu-NSFs effectively inhibited the growth of E. coli. Furthermore, a filtration device incorporating the Cu-NSF-impregnated cheesecloth exhibited reproducible and practical inactivation of E. coli, highlighting its potential for low-cost, scalable water purification applications. Furthermore, the nanostructures remained stable after immersion in water for 12 h, demonstrating the potential of this approach for low-cost, scalable water purification and antimicrobial applications.

item.title: Isotopic Control of Safranin O Photophysics Revealed by Combined Spectroscopy–DFT Analysis and Validated in Energized Mitochondrial Membrane Models
item.description:
Abstract
Isotopic effects on dye photophysics play a central role in interpreting experiments involving singlet oxygen generation, and in the specific case of safranin O, they are particularly important for accurately assessing mitochondrial transmembrane potential. By integrating spectroscopy, singlet-oxygen kinetics, quantum-yield measurements, isotopic substitution, and DFT-based solvation modeling, we show that D2O enhances safranin O fluorescence not by modifying its excitation properties but by suppressing nonradiative decay pathways following excitation. Experiments in ΔpH-energized mitochondrial membrane models reveal that photoexcited safranin O induces minimal photodamage compared with methylene blue, consistent with its substantially lower singlet-oxygen quantum yield and confirming its suitability for bioenergetic applications. The combined computational–experimental analysis provides a mechanistic foundation for the D2O effect and strengthens the photophysical rationale for using safranin O in mitochondrial studies.

item.title: Swelling-Loaded Polystyrene Beads as Size-Defined Conjugated Polymer Emitters for Imaging and Diagnostics
item.description:
Abstract
Conjugated polymer nanoparticles (CPNs) are bright fluorescent probes, but their size, size distribution and surface chemistry are defined by the self-assembly of the polymer, which limits size control and causes aggregation-induced changes in emission. Here, we decouple particle size from polymer self-assembly by loading a conjugated polymer, poly(2,5-di(hexyloxy)cyanoterephthalylidene) (CN-PPV), into preformed, commercially available polystyrene beads (50 nm to 10 μm) using a solvent swelling/deswelling procedure. The loaded beads retain the green, inherent emission of CN-PPV, in contrast to the red, aggregate-type emission of CN-PPV CPNs prepared by nanoprecipitation, consistent with the polymer being dispersed within the rigid polystyrene matrix. The loaded 200 nm beads retain the size and narrow size distribution of the parent beads, and no change in size is seen by electron microscopy for the larger beads, whereas the hydrodynamic diameter of the 50 nm beads increases after loading, consistent with surface-associated polymer and/or partial aggregation. Loaded 50 nm carboxylated beads give strong fluorescence in HeLa cells, and loaded 200 nm carboxylated beads were coupled to antibodies through their surface carboxyl groups and used as reporters in a Neisseria gonorrhoeae lateral flow test. Swelling-based loading therefore offers a simple route to size-defined conjugated polymer emitters with well-defined surface chemistry, particularly for diagnostic formats.

item.title: Stoichiometry-Driven Synthesis of Magnetically Frustrated Complexes
item.description:
Abstract
Quantum spin liquids (QSL) rely on topological frustration, which is sometimes challenging to achieve in coordination compounds. Here, we exploit controlled self-assembly and in situ oxidation of a metal to create a crystalline, deeply frustrated (f = 202) Eu formate complex. The triangular lattice bears a chelate dipole orientation that exacerbates frustration. A large negative Curie–Weiss temperature (−364 K) and strongly suppressed magnetic response under applied fields are consistent with this compound as a candidate QSL, pending exclusion of long-range order and spin freezing via low-temperature heat capacity and susceptibility measurements. Felicitous choice of reactant ratios enables us to precipitate well-ordered triangular lattice compounds with mono- [Eu(μ-O2CH)3]n (1) or di- [Eu(μ-OCHO)(OH)(O2CH)2]2 (2) metallic vertex centers. Head-to-tail (parallel) alignment of the ligand dipoles in (1) presents an enhanced Coulombic shielding, rendering associated Eu2+ spins isolated despite μeff = 5.07 μB. In (2), however, pairwise antiparallel alignment leads to net zero moment and no shielding, resulting in a paramagnetic compound with a measured μeff = 8.36 μB (calculated free-ion value for expected 7/2 spin is 7.94 μB). Homologous Gd (paramagnetic, f < 5) and Sm (candidate frustrated paramagnet, f = 10) complexes confirm this synthetic versatility, establishing a tunable route to spin isolation with possible long-term relevance to quantum processing. This work demonstrates that simplicity and felicitous choice of reaction parameters enable the development of magnetically frustrated materials compatible with automated synthesis, i.e., a synthetically simple, ligand-free formic acid route (simplicity) gives rise to a complex, frustrated antiferromagnetic-type magnetic response (emergent complexity).

item.title: Mixed-Valent Ce/Mn–H 2 BPDC MOF@g-C 3 N 4 Z-Scheme Photocatalyst for Visible-Light Ciprofloxacin Degradation: Experimental and DFT Mechanistic Studies
item.description:
Abstract
This work reports the rational design of a novel mixed-valent Ce–Mn–H2BPDC metal–organic framework (MOF) integrated with graphitic carbon nitride (GCN) to construct a visible-light-responsive direct Z-scheme heterojunction for efficient photocatalytic degradation of ciprofloxacin (CIP). The Ce–Mn–H2BPDC@GCN composite was synthesized through a facile solvothermal-assisted self-assembly strategy and comprehensively characterized, which was supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the successful formation of a mixed-valent Ce3+/Ce4+ and Mn2+/Mn3+/Mn4+ bimetallic framework intimately coupled with GCN nanosheets, providing abundant interfacial contact and enhanced visible-light absorption. Under visible-light irradiation, Ce–Mn–H2BPDC achieved 82% CIP degradation within 120 min, with a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.00543 min–1 (R2 = 0.9937). In contrast, Ce–Mn–H2BPDC@GCN showed enhanced activity, achieving 91% degradation with a higher rate constant of 0.00614 min–1 (R2 = 0.9831). Moreover, Ce–Mn–H2BPDC@GCN maintained most of its photocatalytic activity over five consecutive cycles, demonstrating good recyclability and stability. The radical trapping experiments proved •O2– to be the dominant reactive species, followed by •OH and h+, and the mechanism was supported by direct Z-scheme charge transfer. The HOMO–LUMO, molecular electrostatic potential, density of states, and Fukui function analyses, computed RMSD of electron and hole, Δr intex, H index, and t index singlet and triplet states from DFT calculations, displayed the preferred reactive sites of CIP and provided molecular-level insight into the degradation pathway. The synergistic effects of mixed-valence metal centers, efficient interfacial charge separation, broadened visible-light harvesting, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation collectively account for the outstanding photocatalytic activity. This work presents an effective strategy for designing advanced MOF-based heterojunction photocatalysts for sustainable antibiotic wastewater remediation.

item.title: Fingerprinting, Chemical Constituents, and Quality Control of Dracocephalum tanguticum Maxim. Based on HPLC and UPLC-MS/MS
item.description:
Abstract
This study employed high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), ultraperformance liquid chromatography coupled with Orbitrap high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), fingerprinting, and chemometric methods to systematically analyze 37 batches of wild Dracocephalum tanguticum Maxim. samples collected from Xizang. A characteristic HPLC fingerprint was established, and UPLC-MS/MS was used for the rapid identification of chemical constituents. Potential quality markers were preliminarily selected based on high-resolution mass spectrometry data and literature review, followed by quantification across all samples. Principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) were conducted using R to evaluate the quality variation among different origins based on the contents of selected quality markers. The results showed that 32 common peaks were extracted from the 37 batches, with considerable variability in the similarity among samples. A total of 53 compounds were identified, and 9 quality markers were ultimately screened through comparison with reference standards and MS interpretation. PCA based on these nine markers revealed that the first two principal components (PC1 and PC2) explained 53.3% of the total variance, effectively capturing the structural differences among the samples. Furthermore, HCA heatmaps combined with K-means clustering results demonstrated that the 37 batches could be grouped into three major clusters, which were highly consistent with PCA-based classification, confirming the reliability of the clustering. These findings provide a theoretical and data-based foundation for quality evaluation, grading control, and origin traceability of D. tanguticum, offering support for quality assurance in food and pharmaceutical industries.

item.title: In Silico Prediction of Bacterial Reverse Mutagenicity in Emerging Synthetic Cannabinoids: Implications for Early Carcinogenic Risk Assessment
item.description:
Abstract
Synthetic cannabinoids (SCs) are a structurally diverse class of new psychoactive substances with scarce toxicological data and rapidly evolving structures that challenge risk assessment. This study applied the CASE Ultra, version 1.9.0.8 expert system to predict the genotoxic potential of 18 SCs identified in Brazilian seizures and the literature, and to evaluate how subtle structural modifications may influence mutagenicity-related alerts. Predictions were generated combining the GT_EXPERT (rule-based), GT1_BMUT (statistical bacterial reverse mutagenicity model), and the integrated Konsolidator module. For each compound, the software provided positive, negative, or inconclusive outputs, identifying structural alerts and deactivating fragments, as well as listed database analogs. Inconclusive or conflicting results underwent expert review considering structural similarity, DNA accessibility, metabolic plausibility, and supporting evidence. Compounds showing positive or inconclusive outcomes were further evaluated using three complementary QSAR platforms (VEGA Hub version 1.1.5, Toxtree 3.1.0, and OECD QSAR Toolbox version 4.8) to assess the consistency of structural alerts across different computational approaches. Whenever available, predictions were interpreted in light of published experimental data. Most SCs were classified as negative by the integrated CASE Ultra prediction, suggesting an overall low predicted bacterial reverse mutagenicity risk within the evaluated group. JWH-018 was the only compound consistently classified as positive, whereas CH-FUBIATA yielded an inconclusive prediction due to the coexistence of activating and deactivating structural features. Comparative analysis demonstrated good agreement between CASE Ultra and VEGA Hub, with both platforms identifying similar mutagenicity-associated structural alerts for JWH-018 and CH-FUBIATA. In contrast, neither Toxtree nor the OECD QSAR Toolbox identified structural alerts for these compounds, likely reflecting the limited representation of contemporary SCs within their underlying knowledge bases. A simulated structural modification of PX-2 demonstrated that removal of a deactivating amine group converted a negative prediction into a positive one, illustrating how minor chemical changes may substantially alter predicted genotoxic risk. Conversely, the predicted metabolites of PX-1 and PX-2 retained negative classifications, indicating that molecular modifications do not inherently alter mutagenic potential and that distinct structural changes, whether resulting from deliberate chemical modification or metabolic biotransformation, may lead to different genotoxicity outcomes. These findings demonstrate that predicted bacterial reverse mutagenicity is determined by the interaction between activating and deactivating structural features within the overall molecular architecture rather than by isolated pharmacophoric elements. The concordance observed between CASE Ultra and VEGA Hub supports the mechanistic interpretation of the identified structural alerts, whereas the absence of alerts in other expert systems underscores the need to expand QSAR training data sets for emerging substances. Overall, integrated in silico approaches represent valuable tools for the early prioritization of toxicological risks, although further experimental validation remains essential to strengthen predictive confidence.

item.title: Vertical Differentiation of Aromatic Hydrocarbon Geochemistry in the Fengcheng Formation Shale Oil Interval: A Case Study of Well Xia 207
item.description:
Abstract
To clarify the vertical differentiation of aromatic hydrocarbon compositions in shale oil intervals and its implications for favorable-interval evaluation, 64 valid core samples were collected from the Fengcheng Formation interval at 4759.71–5010.67 m in Well Xia 207, northern Mahu Sag, Junggar Basin. Group-fraction separation and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) analysis of the aromatic fractions were conducted, and the compositional data were further processed using the centered log-ratio transformation and principal component analysis (PCA). The results show that the aromatic fractions are dominated by the phenanthrene series, which accounts for 48.318–83.558% of the integrated aromatic hydrocarbons, with an average of 70.457%. The naphthalene, chrysene, fluorene–dibenzothiophene–dibenzofuran, and triaromatic steroid series exhibit pronounced vertical variations. The methylphenanthrene parameters F1 and F2 range from 0.403 to 0.574 and from 0.227 to 0.333, respectively. The equivalent vitrinite reflectance calculated from the methylphenanthrene index shows a good correlation with the measured vitrinite reflectance (Ro) (R2 = 0.87, n = 22). Together with other maturity indicators, these results suggest that the studied interval is generally within the mature oil-generation stage. Using the C1–C12 sublayers as the stratigraphic framework, and considering the vertical transitions and continuity of multiple aromatic assemblages, the studied interval was subdivided into six aromatic geochemical assemblage zones, AGZ-1 to AGZ-6. The first three principal components cumulatively explain 85.21% of the total variance in aromatic composition, indicating recognizable multivariate compositional differences among the assemblage zones. The C9–C10 interval, identified as a major sweet-spot interval in the evaluation of the study area, corresponds to AGZ-5. This zone has the highest average phenanthrene content and an overall relatively concentrated aromatic composition, together with a relative increase in C26 triaromatic steroids, indicating molecular compositional adjustment within the sweet-spot interval. Naphthalene and low-substituted naphthalenes show a degree of covariation with intervals characterized by high Rock-Eval free hydrocarbon contents (S1). Together with the response of methyl dibenzothiophene parameters, this relationship suggests that the occurrence of free hydrocarbons and differential partitioning between light and heavy aromatic hydrocarbons may jointly influence local aromatic compositions. These features provide auxiliary evidence for identifying heterogeneity and microscale fractionation within the sweet-spot interval, but they are insufficient to independently determine the direction of shale oil micromigration. The results provide a basis for vertical geochemical zoning, detailed correlation within the main sweet-spot interval, and molecular-scale heterogeneity evaluation of Fengcheng Formation shale oil.

item.title: Vanillin-Cross-linked Chitosan/Guar Gum Films Functionalized with Silver Nanoparticles for Active Food Packaging
item.description:
Abstract
Chitosan/guar gum (CS/GG) composite films were prepared by combining vanillin modification with silver nanoparticle (AgNP) incorporation for potential application in active food packaging. Vanillin promoted network formation through Schiff-base formation and hydrogen-bond interactions, whereas AgNPs provided antibacterial functionality. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy supported the formation of imine (C═N) linkages within the CS/GG matrix. The film containing 0.3% (w/v) vanillin exhibited the highest tensile strength (57.9 MPa), whereas further addition reduced film flexibility. Vanillin modification also improved barrier performance and UV shielding. Incorporation of 120 μL AgNP suspension (82.13 mg/L) into the selected formulation produced the highest bacterial growth inhibition under the assay conditions, reaching 54.0% against Staphylococcus aureus and 69.0% against Escherichia coli. During 7 days of refrigerated pork storage, the CS/GG/V-0.3/AgNPs60 film reduced mass loss, limited the increase in pH, and better maintained visual appearance compared with the unsealed and AgNP-free controls. Soil burial testing showed mass losses of 68.8–82.1% after 14 days, with lower final mass loss in the AgNP-containing films. Overall, vanillin modification improved the mechanical, barrier, and UV-shielding properties of CS/GG films, while subsequent AgNP incorporation enhanced antibacterial activity. The selected AgNP-containing film also demonstrated quality-retention benefits during refrigerated pork storage.

item.title: Dual-Reporter Signal-Off Aptamer-Based Sensing for Enhanced Vancomycin Detection
item.description:
Abstract
The translation of electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors into real-world applications, including continuous therapeutic drug monitoring, remains limited by low sensitivity and poor stability in physiological conditions. EAB sensors typically rely on a single redox reporter covalently attached to the aptamer to transduce target-induced conformational changes into an electrochemical signal. To date, efforts to improve EAB sensor performance have focused on aptamer engineering, optimizing immobilization and backfilling strategies, and selection of redox reporters. However, strategies capable of enhancing sensitivity beyond this established single-reporter configuration remain limited. Here, we report a dual-reporter EAB sensing strategy that exploits microenvironmental changes around two redox reporters within the sensing layer to improve vancomycin detection. The sensing interface combines an Os(II)-labeled vancomycin aptamer and a surface-immobilized MB moiety covalently anchored to an alkanethiol-based mixed monolayer. We propose that the vancomycin-induced conformational change in the aptamer modulates the local redox environment of the Os(II) complex and MB. Upon target binding, the square-wave voltammetric currents of both redox reporters decrease concomitantly, resulting in a dual-signal-OFF response with enhanced analytical performance. The proposed system achieves a 19-fold lower limit of detection than the corresponding single-reporter configuration using the Os(II)-labeled aptamer. Overall, these results identify a powerful and underexplored signal-transduction mechanism, introducing a new design paradigm for enhancing the sensitivity of EAB sensors.

item.title: Microfibrillated Cellulose as a Reinforcement Agent in Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate (ASA) for MEX 3D Printing: A Thermomechanical and Rheological Filler Content Assessment
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, acrylonitrile styrene acrylate (ASA), a thermoplastic with great resistance to weather conditions, was combined with the nature-sourced microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) to produce composites with improved properties in additive manufacturing (AM). Filament extrusion was used to fabricate the filaments. The test specimens were 3D printed for thermal, rheological, dynamic mechanical, and mechanical characterization. The thermal behavior was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry, while the rheological performance was evaluated through viscosity and material flow rate measurements. The effect of MFC on quality metrics (dimensional accuracy and porosity) was also assessed using microcomputed tomography. Among the five composites investigated (0.5–2.5 wt % MFC, step 0.5 wt %), the 1.5 wt % sample showed the best overall performance, except in Vickers microhardness. Compared with pure ASA, this composite improved tensile strength and toughness, flexural toughness, and Charpy impact strength by approximately 13%, tensile modulus by 15%, flexural modulus by 12%, and flexural strength by approximately 28%. The highest Vickers microhardness was achieved by the 1.0 wt % composite, showing a 30.8% increase over pure ASA. Overall, the introduction of the biobased MFC, even at low loadings, enhanced the mechanical strength of ASA and improved the quality metrics. Such findings highlight the potential of ASA/MFC as a sustainable composite for outdoor 3D printing applications.

item.title: Structure–Activity Relationship and Molecular Docking Analysis of Flavonoid Analogues Prepared via Divergent Synthesis for Anti-Inflammatory Activity
item.description:
Abstract
Flavonoids are heterocyclic compounds that possess significant pharmacological properties, particularly anti-inflammatory activities. However, the development of eco-friendly synthetic methods for these compounds and the systematic study of their structure–activity relationships (SAR) remain essential areas of focus in medicinal chemistry. Thus, a highly efficient, green divergence synthesis was developed for the selective preparation of flavanones and flavones under microwave irradiation using DI water as an environmentally friendly solvent. A library of flavonoids was evaluated for anti-inflammatory activities by measuring the inflammatory gene expressions (iNOS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and COX-2) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264 macrophage cells using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Structure–activity relationship (SAR) investigations identified that a methyl group at the C-7 position (para position with the carbonyl group on ring A of the flavonoid) and at the C-4′ position on ring B, combined with a double bond on ring C, significantly enhanced anti-inflammatory activity. The optimized flavone 4b exhibited strong anti-inflammatory properties, effectively blocking iNOS (30.29%), IL-1β (13.18%), TNF-α (15.01%), and COX-2 (13.20%) mRNA expression to similar or better levels than the commercial dexamethasone drug and baicalein positive control. An in silico study was conducted to explain the interaction between the binding site and the developed compounds, as well as the structure–activity relationship (SAR) of the flavonoid moiety.

item.title: N-Alkylation of Amides with Benzylic Alcohols Catalyzed by a Cationic Ruthenium(II) Complex
item.description:
Abstract
A ruthenium(II) complex, [(η6-p-cymene)Ru(bpm)Cl]+[PF6]− (1) {bpm = bis(3,5-dimethylpyrazolyl)methane} has been synthesized and structurally characterized. The compound crystallizes in the monoclinic space group P21. The compound catalyzes N-alkylation of aromatic amides with benzylic alcohols in the presence of Cs2CO3 in toluene at 120 °C with very good to excellent conversions. Mechanistic investigations were carried out using control experiments, in situ 1H NMR experiments, and mass spectrometric studies.
