item.title: Enhancing Removal of PFAS and Pharmaceuticals from Municipal Wastewater via GAC Pretreatment and StyDex Polishing
item.description:
Abstract
A dual-sorbent system consisting of a granular activated carbon (GAC) pretreatment followed by polishing with styrene-functionalized β-cyclodextrin (StyDex) beads was evaluated for removal of four per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS: PFOA, PFHxA, PFBA and PFHxS) and two pharmaceuticals, bezafibrate (BEZ) and diclofenac (DCF), from municipal wastewater. Building on previous pilot evaluations of StyDex as a stand-alone sorbent, this study evaluates its integration into a treatment train with GAC pretreatment, examining GAC replacement frequency and selection of polishing sorbent to more effectively remove mixtures of PFAS and other trace organic contaminants from municipal wastewater. Upstream GAC pretreatment was used to nonselectively remove target compounds, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and other competing background wastewater constituents to enhance downstream polishing performance. System performance was evaluated by comparing individual removal of target compounds by GAC-StyDex and GAC-ion-exchange resin (IXR) treatment trains and assessing the impact of periodic GAC replacement on polishing performance. Combining GAC pretreatment with StyDex polishing demonstrated the highest total removal of PFOA, PFHxS, and DCF over the duration of the pilot, and improved removal of the weaker sorbing compounds, PFHxA, BEZ, and PFBA. However, PFBA was not effectively controlled over the full pilot duration and exhibited substantially lower cumulative removal (55%–62%) in the GAC-StyDex and GAC-IXR trains, compared to the other five target compounds, which all had >93% removal. Extending the GAC replacement interval from 2,500 to 5,000 BV increased sorption capacity by 59.9% (0.177 to 0.283 μmol g–1), allowing greater GAC bed utilization prior to replacement while also maintaining low effluent concentrations after polishing. Compared with GAC-IXR, GAC-StyDex had 87.4% greater sorption capacity (0.283 vs 0.151 μmol g–1) on a mass-normalized basis and similar performance on a sorbent-volume basis, demonstrating StyDex as a high-capacity alternative sorbent for downstream polishing. These findings demonstrate the potential for integrating GAC pretreatment with downstream polishing to improve contaminant removal, maintain low effluent concentrations, enhance sorbent utilization, and inform the design of scalable wastewater treatment systems.

item.title: Thermodynamics of Exchange Reactions of Heterometallic Mg and Ca Carbonate Nanoclusters
item.description:
Abstract
Density functional theory (DFT) and correlated molecular orbital theory (CCSD(T)) methods were used to investigate aqueous-phase heterometallic substitution in (MgCO3)n and (CaCO3)n nanoclusters containing two to four MCO3, yielding (M′CO3)(MCO3)(n−1) clusters (n = 2−4), where M = Mg or Ca and M′ = Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, or Hg. Solvation free energies were predicted using the CPCM model, a self-consistent reaction field (SCRF) method. The Mg- and Ca-based mixed-metal clusters generally prefer structures similar to (MgCO3)n and (CaCO3)n for n = 2−4, with most metal centers having a metal−O coordination number (CN) of 4. Aqueous binding free energies for the isodesmic exchange of M′CO3 units into (MCO3)n were calculated. The binding free energies of the larger alkaline-earth M′CO3 are favorable in the Mg-based and unfavorable in the Ca-based nanoclusters, whereas exchange of most 3d and Group 12 M′CO3 units is favorable, driven mainly by the strong solvation of the MgCO3 and CaCO3 products. The predicted substitution free energies of the hydrated Group 2 and 3d transition and Group 12 metal dications [M(H2O)m]2+ were predicted to correspond with H2O release upon substitution, solvation effects, and ionic radius.

item.title: Green Electrochemical Synthesis of Antimicrobial Polyaldehyde Starch
item.description:
Abstract
Conventional aldehyde-based biocides raise environmental and safety concerns due to their toxicity and persistence in inhibiting microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in numerous industrial applications. The present study introduces a rapid and sustainable method for synthesizing polyaldehyde starch through electrochemistry (PAS-EC) using soluble starch as feedstock in aqueous salt media with iridium–ruthenium electrodes. This approach has the potential to replace toxic oxidants with a safer alternative, while significantly reducing reaction time and enhancing overall process safety. By minimizing hazardous reagents and streamlining operational steps, it can also contribute to improved sustainability. Taken together, these features make electrochemical methods a promising pathway for application in industrial bioprocesses. Under optimized electrochemical conditions (15 mA cm–2, 15% NaCl, and 1 h), PAS-EC was obtained with 65% yield and a degree of oxidation exceeding 63%, surpassing the conventional periodate-oxidized dialdehyde starch (DAS-PO) with 50% yield and a 48% degree of oxidation. FTIR and NMR characterization confirmed the successful formation of aldehydic groups, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed a decrease in thermal stability due to the modification in the structure of pure starch. Biocidal efficacy was assessed against six hydrocarbon-degrading bacterial strains that are extremely relevant to MIC and bioremediation under oil and gas field conditions. PAS-EC displayed promising and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with a maximum of 60% inhibition efficiency at 1000 ppm in comparison to glutaraldehyde. Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

item.title: Tau Disaggregation by a CNS-Permeable Small Molecule Reduces Fibril and Oligomer Burden and Preserves Proteostasis and Behavior
item.description:
Abstract
Pathological aggregates of the microtubule-associated protein, tau, drive neuronal dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related tauopathies. Yet, strategies to slow or eliminate progressive accumulation of misfolded tau protein in the brain remain underdeveloped relative to upstream therapeutic approaches, such as amyloid-beta (Aβ) immunotherapy. Here, we explore a coumarin-based series of brain-permeable small molecules that disaggregate tau. Structure–activity relationships (SAR) identified nitrile-containing analogs as potential leads from the series and suggest a stacking-driven disassembly mechanism. Small molecules from this series disaggregated tau from AD brain-derived matter, reducing aggregate burden measured in vitro across both fibrillar and oligomeric tau species, two principal pathological aggregate species implicated in disease. Mechanistic studies demonstrate that disaggregation does not generate soluble oligomeric intermediates, addressing a central question in the field. Inhibitor treatment reduces prion-like seeding, a disease-related mechanism by which tau aggregation pathology spreads in the brain. The lead candidate from this series is well tolerated in vivo, which enabled efficacy testing in a tauopathy mouse model. Treatment reduced tau pathology while preserving behavioral function, proteasome capacity, and synaptic integrity. These findings establish small-molecule tau disaggregation as a viable therapeutic strategy and provide a mechanistic framework for the design of aggregate-directed therapeutics in neurodegeneration.

item.title: Oxidation of Water and Hydroxide by Graphite Fluoride
item.description:
Abstract
Graphite fluoride is defluorinated by water at high and neutral pH under subcritical conditions. The solid carbon product is unusual in that it is largely graphitic but also contains nanoscale linear hydrocarbon segments. The high pH system is strongly oxidizing, and some carbon is removed as CO32–. Carbon–carbon bonds in partially defluorinated materials are destabilized, and cyclic fluorocarbons are released on heating to as low as 200 °C. The relationship to Li-(CF)x battery technology is discussed.

item.title: Aqueous • OH Kinetics of Gluconic, Glucuronic, and Galacturonic Acids and Lifetimes in Cloudwater
item.description:
Abstract
Reactions of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) with organic compounds strongly influence the formation and evolution of organic aerosols, cloudwater chemistry, and the oxidative capacity of water in natural and engineered environments. In this work, bimolecular reaction rate constants (kOH, M–1 s–1) for aqueous •OH reaction with the environmentally widespread sugar acids (SAs): gluconic, glucuronic, and galacturonic acids in the temperature range between 278 and 318 K were measured. The measurements were performed with the laser flash photolysis–long-path absorption technique for undissociated (AH) and dissociated (A¯) forms of SAs. At 298 K, the measured kOH values ranged from 1.0 to 1.3 × 109 M–1 s–1, with higher reactivity observed for carboxylates. The values of activation parameters were characteristic of the •OH reaction with saturated water-soluble organic compounds (WSOCs) and revealed an enthalpy (ΔH‡)–entropy (ΔS‡) compensation for AH and A¯ forms of SAs. A¯ forms of SAs exhibited lower activation energies, ΔH‡, and more negative ΔS‡ values, uncharacteristic of other C4–C6 saturated acids. Such behavior was consistent with long-range effects of acid dissociation, potentially involving electronic, conformational, and H-bonding effects. kOH values predicted for SAs with two structure–activity relationships (SARs) were overestimated up to 3.5 times, due to the lack of parametrization for the unique electronic effects of adjacent −OH moieties. The intramolecular selectivity of •OH reaction with SAs was analyzed with SARs and density functional theory (DFT). Both methods indicated a preferential H atom abstraction by •OH from the C–H bonds further away from the acidic moiety. DFT results showed that −COOH dissociation affects the energy barriers for H atom abstraction through the (poly)hydroxylated carbon chain, consistent with a long-range electronic effect. Obtained kinetic data revealed that the •OH reaction with SAs can contribute to their removal in remote, marine, and some urban clouds. The reported results provide new kinetic data for the •OH reaction with highly oxygenated molecules, thereby facilitating the development of SARs and atmospheric models.

item.title: Coupled Mechanisms of Surrounding Rock Stability and Spontaneous Combustion Control in Gob-Side Entry Retaining under Fully Mechanized Top Coal Caving
item.description:
Abstract
The safety of gob-side entry retaining (GER) in fully mechanized top coal caving (FMTC) panels involves the interacting evolution of surrounding rock deformation, roadside backfill body (RBB) damage, air leakage, oxygen migration, and residual coal oxidation. However, the mechanical origin of leakage channel formation and its connection with spontaneous combustion risk remain insufficiently clarified. This study investigates the 090515 working face of Duanwang Coal Mine and develops a fracture-mediated framework linking top coal–RBB load transfer, RBB damage evolution, goaf air leakage, oxygen distribution, and carbon monoxide (CO) response. An analytical load-transfer model was established to clarify the role of top coal in the local bearing system, while three-dimensional discrete-element simulation was used to examine RBB fracture development and structural degradation. Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) tracer tests were conducted to quantify the spatial attenuation of goaf air leakage, and laboratory oxidation tests and field gas monitoring were used to identify the site-specific oxidation-prone zone. The results indicate that insufficient top coal stiffness and progressive RBB damage are associated with deterioration of the local bearing and sealing system, while stronger leakage is observed in the near-face region. The measured SF6-derived apparent leakage velocity decreases with distance from the working face, allowing the leakage field to be divided into a high-variability zone, a transitional-attenuation zone, and a relatively stable low-velocity zone. Based on closed oxygen consumption tests and field gas monitoring, the 12–18% oxygen concentration range was adopted as a site-specific criterion for identifying the oxidation-prone zone in the 090515 goaf. Field application indicates that the integrated control strategy was associated with reduced roadway deformation and a short-term decrease in CO concentration during the available monitoring period. The findings provide a field-supported basis for coordinated control of surrounding rock stability and spontaneous combustion risk in FMTC conditions with GER.

item.title: Nanoarchitectonics-Enabled Multifunctional Hydrogel with Artesunate-Loaded Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles for Accelerated Diabetic Wound Healing via JAK1/STAT3-Mediated Macrophage Reprogramming
item.description:
Abstract
Diabetic wound healing is critically hindered by persistent macrophage dysfunction, characterized by an inability to transition from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the pro-healing M2 phenotype. Artesunate (ART) holds therapeutic promise for immunomodulation, yet its clinical translation is constrained by poor aqueous solubility and lack of sustained local delivery. Inspired by the concept of nanoarchitectonics, a post-nanotechnology paradigm that constructs functional material systems through the deliberate orchestration of atoms, molecules, and nanomaterials, we herein architect a multifunctional composite hydrogel (TA/CMCS/OSA/MSN@ART) via an integrated multi-step assembly strategy. This nanoarchitectonic design hierarchically integrates molecular building blocks, carboxymethyl chitosan, oxidized sodium alginate, and tannic acid, through Schiff-base dynamic covalent crosslinking and supramolecular hydrogen bonding, while simultaneously embedding ART-loaded mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSN@ART) as functional nanoscale units within the porous scaffold. This hydrogel demonstrates favorable physicochemical characteristics and exhibits notable biological properties, including low hemolysis, potent antibacterial and antioxidant activities, and high biocompatibility. Importantly, the ART-loaded hydrogel significantly accelerates diabetic wound healing by facilitating macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype. This effect appears to be closely associated with the activation of the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway. These findings establish nanoarchitectonics as a powerful and versatile methodology for designing advanced biomaterials, offering a transformative strategy for the management of chronic diabetic wounds.

item.title: Branched Poly- l -Lysine Molecules for the Delivery of Nucleic Acids
item.description:
Abstract
Gene therapy is a rapidly expanding area of research, with a growing number of publications and clinical trials since the advent of the field. Despite substantial advances, one of the most significant roadblocks faced during gene therapy is the failure to efficiently deliver genetic material into target cells at levels sufficient to achieve a therapeutic effect. Therefore, an active and crucial area of research is the development of gene therapy platforms that can efficiently and safely transfect cells with low levels of cytotoxicity and immunogenicity. Toward this, cationic polymers offer a desirable platform due to their ability to self-complex with genetic material, ability to transfect cells, their ease and controllability of production, and their low immunogenicity. Though cationic polymers can induce some level of toxicity due to their positive charge and, display lower transfection efficacy compared to virus-based gene transfection agents, alterations can be made to the polymers (i.e., charge, molecular architecture, molecular weight, etc.) to help increase their transfection efficiency and mitigate drawbacks. In this study, we explored such alterations with a cationic polymer, branched poly-l-lysine (BPL), with lysine as the repeating unit, for their ability to transfect cells using plasmid DNA (pDNA) as genetic material.

item.title: A Label-Free Method to Quantify Early Stage Amyloid Aggregation via Intrinsic Phenylalanine Fluorescence
item.description:
Abstract
The aggregation of amyloid-forming peptides is a dynamic, complex process that underlies their diverse biological activities, from physiological functions to disease-associated dysfunctions. While the structure of fibrillar end-products is well-characterized for most amyloids, the heterogeneous and often transient oligomers, likely key in cytotoxicity, remain poorly investigated, especially for peptides with low-yield aromatic residues. Here, by exploiting and developing flow induced dispersion analysis in both peak and front modes, we demonstrate that intrinsic phenylalanine fluorescence can be harnessed to quantify the conversion of diffusing monomers into nondiffusing oligomers and fibrils. This approach is validated using PSMα3, a tryptophan- and tyrosine-free peptide from S. aureus, known for its fast amyloid fibrillation and key roles in bacterial virulence. We indeed characterize its low-molecular-weight oligomers, and size evolution from 2 to 10 nm over time. Importantly, to further validate the robustness of our front-mode approach, we apply it to hIAPP, a tyrosine-containing, tryptophan-free peptide, with critical outcome in type 2 diabetes. Our results overcome the limitations of traditional biochemical and biophysical amyloid assays by extending analysis from large oligomers and fibrils to small heterogeneous oligomers, under near-physiological conditions. This study thus offers a new analytical framework, thereby filling a critical gap in amyloid research, to probe the early stages of aggregation, key in the design of alternative therapeutics for amyloid-diseases.

item.title: DFT Study of NH 3 Adsorption and Decomposition on Zr(0001)
item.description:
Abstract
Ammonia adsorption and decomposition to hydrogen and nitrogen is studied on the Zr(0001) surface using density functional theory within the generalized gradient approximation and a supercell approach at a coverage of 0.25 ML. Different adsorption sites are considered for NH3 and its dehydrogenated species. We find that ammonia adsorbs readily and decomposes to atomic nitrogen and hydrogen through an exothermic pathway with relatively small kinetic barriers. The NH decomposition step is identified as rate-limiting. Nitrogen strongly favors subsurface incorporation over surface adsorption, whereas hydrogen remains on the surface. The reaction energetics and kinetic barriers obtained in this work are compared with previous studies of NH3 adsorption and decomposition via sequential hydrogen abstraction on ZrB2(0001).

item.title: Dependent Morphological Transformation of Sc-MOFs with Boosted Catalytic Performance
item.description:
Abstract
The coordination modulation method of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is intensively researched for creating new materials with highly controlled particle size and morphology because these factors strongly influence the abilities of gas separation, adsorption, and catalysis. Most of the research focuses on the ratio of modulators and the type of reagent. However, this approach does not necessarily optimize the structures, which reduces the potential of the materials. In this study, we investigated the effect of reaction time on the particle morphologies and revealed the mechanism of morphological changes from dodecahedron structures to flower-like structures. According to more detailed studies, this was attributed to the amount of acetic acid, the formation of sheet-like structures, and aggregation. Furthermore, flower-like structures have higher catalytic performance than dodecahedron-like structures. In addition, flower-like structures displayed a type IV adsorption isotherm unlike dodecahedron-like structures displaying type I. Therefore, this approach based on reaction time and the mechanism could lead to new MOFs with outstanding properties.

item.title: Optimization of Sensor Response Time in Microfluidics-Based Biosensors with Balanced Analyte Transport
item.description:
Abstract
The combined effect of geometric obstruction and auxiliary inlet on sensor response time for a microfluidics-integrated biosensor has been numerically investigated in this study. The flow behavior and mass transfer of an analyte have been modeled using incompressible Navier–Stokes equations coupled with convection–diffusion and Langmuir adsorption kinetics equations for comparable time scales of diffusion and surface reaction. Introduction of a block increases the analyte velocity near the sensor surface with subsequent reduction in diffusion boundary layer thickness, thereby ameliorating the sensor response time. Insertion of an auxiliary inlet diminishes the sensor response time to a greater extent by confining a thin layer of analyte above the sensor surface. A systematic parametric study is conducted to evaluate the blended effects of block height, block position, block width, auxiliary inlet position, and auxiliary inlet velocity on sensor performance. Taguchi-based optimization techniques employing an L27 orthogonal array alongside signal-to-noise ratio analysis and analysis of variance have been utilized for identification of optimal parameter combinations. The results indicate that the auxiliary inlet velocity is the most influential parameter with a contribution of 65.8% toward the decrement in sensor response time. The findings demonstrate that the combination of block-induced flow-field modifications and auxiliary-inlet-mediated flow confinement effect significantly augments analyte transport to the sensor surface, thereby decreasing the sensor response time by approximately 92% in comparison to the scenario devoid of a block and auxiliary inlet. This study provides valuable insights for the design and optimization of point-of-care microfluidic devices with reduced detection time.

item.title: Experimental Study on the Seepage Characteristics of Rough Single Fracture in Limestone under Stress–Seepage Pressure Condition
item.description:
Abstract
In complex engineering geological environments, rock masses are subjected to the long-term coupled effects of geostress and groundwater seepage, and their permeability characteristics play a critical role in engineering stability. Taking limestone from the engineering site as the research material, through-going single-fracture specimens with different fracture roughness levels were prepared using the Brazilian splitting method. Three-dimensional laser scanning of fracture morphology and multicondition single-fracture seepage tests were conducted. A systematic method for characterizing the 3D roughness of fracture surfaces was established, and the combined effects of confining pressure, seepage pressure, and fracture roughness on the permeability coefficient were investigated. The results indicate that (1) the single-fracture seepage in each designed test condition is in a laminar flow state, and the fracture permeability coefficient can be calculated using the cubic law. (2) The fracture roughness can be quantified using the surface roughness ratio Rs and the root-mean-square of the first derivative Z2, and their consistency indicates that Z2 can serve as an equivalent roughness descriptor relative to Rs. (3) Under confining pressures of 2.0 and 5.0 MPa and at injection flow rates of 2.0 mL/min and 3.0 mL/min, the permeability coefficient of the fractures increased significantly with increasing fracture roughness. The permeability coefficient was negatively correlated with confining pressure, and its variation with increasing confining pressure could be divided into three stages: “rapid decrease–gradual decrease–quasi-stable”. A positive correlation was observed between the permeability coefficient and the ratio of flow pressure Q/ps. (4) Based on data fitting, a quasi-exponential relationship among the permeability coefficient, effective stress, and fracture roughness was established, quantitatively characterizing the coupled interaction between the stress field and seepage field. These findings provide a theoretical basis for evaluating seepage stability in rock engineering.

item.title: In Silico Discovery of Novel Topoisomerase IIα Inhibitors with Enhanced Antiproliferative Activity in Breast Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
Human topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) is frequently overexpressed in aggressive cancers, making it an attractive therapeutic target. Herein, we employed an integrated in silico and experimental approach to identify novel TOP2A inhibitors. A library of 669,069 filtered, drug-like bioactive small molecules from PubChem was screened against human TOP2A (PDB ID: 5GWK) using Schrödinger Maestro with Glide SP and XP docking, yielding 202 compounds with docking scores superior to etoposide. Subsequent filtering for PAINS, ADMET, and selectivity assessment against other human type I and type II topoisomerases yielded 21 ligands. Docking against multidomain TOP2A (PDB ID: 6ZY8) revealed preferential binding at the DNA-gate over the ATP-binding N-gate region, with L8 (pitavastatin) achieving the highest docking score. Based on their docking score, selectivity, and commercial availability, five ligands were selected for experimental evaluation. A cell viability assay showed that pitavastatin and L21 (PubChem CID: 7369491) exhibited potent cytotoxicity against MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 breast cancer cells, respectively, with reduced toxicity against normal HEK293 cells. Both ligands induced S-phase arrest and late apoptosis in MDA-MB-231 cells, with pitavastatin outperforming etoposide. The in vitro plasmid relaxation assay confirmed that all five ligands inhibited TOP2A activity consistent with the poison mechanism, while pitavastatin exhibited a nonintercalative mode of binding to DNA. Molecular dynamics simulations for pitavastatin supported stable binding within the TOP2A active site. These findings identify pitavastatin as a promising repurposed candidate for TOP2A-targeted therapy, particularly against the triple-negative breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231.

item.title: Fabrication of Vitamin E-Loaded Rhamnolipid Nanoemulsion for Antioxidant and Selective-Cleansing Applications
item.description:
Abstract
With the growing demand for mild precision skincare, conventional synthetic surfactant-based facial cleansers nonselectively strip both sebum triglycerides (TG) and skin-barrier lipids (ceramides, cholesterol), resulting in barrier impairment, skin dryness, and oxidative damage. Biosurfactant rhamnolipid (Rha) exhibits amphiphilic properties, yet pure Rha nanocarriers suffer from poor colloidal stability and limited antioxidant protection. In this work, we aimed to construct pea-protein-isolate-stabilized Rha nanoemulsion (Rha-PPI-HS-VE) for vitamin E (VE) delivery, achieving dual functions of UV-oxidative-stress protection and lipid-selective cleansing. The pH-shift-treated unfolded pea-protein isolate (PPI) was assembled with rhamnolipid, using hemisqualane (HS) as an oil core to solubilize VE. After process optimization, a monodisperse nanoemulsion was obtained with particle size of 108.5 nm, polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.128, and a high VE encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 99.73 ± 0.03%. In vitro assays showed that 10% sample achieved 63.91% DPPH and 88.20% ABTS radical-scavenging rates (SR) and retained most antioxidant activity after 90-day storage. In UVB-damaged HaCaT keratinocytes, Rha-PPI-HS-VE (0.32%) markedly alleviated oxidative stress (the intracellular fluorescence of reactive-oxygen-species (ROS) probe decreased from 11,340 to 4722) and restored mitochondrial membrane potential. When incorporated into cleansing formulation, the nanoemulsion removed up to 86.16% triglyceride while preserving ceramides and cholesterol without significant loss. This study demonstrates that PPI-Rha biopolymer nanoemulsion can serve as a multifunctional green carrier, offering technical support for developing next-generation mild cleansing cosmetic raw materials with antioxidant-repair and selective-lipid-regulating functions.

item.title: Folate-Functionalized PAMAM–Nanodiamond Conjugates for Sustained pH-Dependent Cabazitaxel Release and Enhanced Cytotoxicity in Prostate Cancer Cells
item.description:
Abstract
Cabazitaxel (CTX) is an effective chemotherapeutic agent for advanced prostate cancer, but limited aqueous solubility and systemic toxicity motivate alternative delivery strategies. Herein, we developed a folate receptor-targeted nanodiamond-based nanoconjugate (ND-PAMAM-FA-CTX) for selective and controlled drug delivery. Cabazitaxel was first converted to CTX-hemisuccinate and subsequently conjugated to a fourth-generation polyamidoamine (PAMAM) dendrimer along with folic acid (FA), followed by covalent attachment to nanodiamonds (NDs). Comprehensive physicochemical characterization confirmed the successful construction of the nanoconjugate while preserving the structural integrity of the nanodiamond core. The resulting platform exhibited high CTX-loading capacity and a sustained, pH-responsive drug-release profile, with enhanced release under acidic conditions relevant to the tumor microenvironment. The drug-free carrier showed excellent biocompatibility, whereas ND-PAMAM-FA-CTX demonstrated superior anticancer activity against folate receptor (FAR)-overexpressing PC3 prostate cancer cells compared with free CTX and nontargeted controls. Flow cytometry and confocal microscopy revealed significantly enhanced cellular uptake mediated by folate receptor-dependent endocytosis, which was further confirmed through competitive inhibition studies using free folic acid. Moreover, ND-PAMAM-FA-CTX exhibited a low nanomolar IC50 value (∼5 nM) and markedly suppressed PC3 cell migration. Overall, these findings demonstrate that ND-PAMAM-FA-CTX is a promising targeted nanotherapeutic platform that combines selective cellular delivery and controlled drug release with enhanced efficacy, offering potential for future targeted chemotherapy applications.

item.title: Injectable Curcumin-Loaded Gellan Gum/Pea Protein Isolate Hydrogels Reinforced with Different Calcium Phosphate Phases: Physicochemical Properties, Drug Release, and Antibacterial Activity
item.description:
Abstract
Chronic bone infection remains challenging to treat because limited drug penetration and impaired tissue regeneration can compromise therapeutic outcomes, highlighting the need for effective localized treatment strategies. In this study, injectable gellan gum/pea protein isolate (GG/PPI) composite hydrogels containing hydroxyapatite (HA), β-tricalcium phosphate (β-TCP), and biphasic calcium phosphate (BCP) were developed and evaluated for their physicochemical properties, injectability, rheological behavior, aqueous stability, and in vitro cytotoxicity. All formulations showed interconnected porous structures with pore sizes of approximately 50–600 μm, substantial water absorption, and successful injection through a 20G needle. Incorporation of calcium phosphate improved the viscoelastic properties of the GG/PPI matrix, with β-TCP/GG/PPI hydrogel showing the highest storage modulus. Cytotoxicity was evaluated using human ovarian follicular fluid-derived mesenchymal stem cells, and all hydrogel extracts maintained cell viability above 70% across the tested concentration range, indicating no pronounced in vitro cytotoxicity. Curcumin was then incorporated to investigate drug release and antibacterial activity. The curcumin-loaded hydrogels showed a biphasic release profile. Cur-β-TCP/GG/PPI hydrogel released curcumin more rapidly and to a greater extent, whereas Cur-HA/GG/PPI and Cur-BCP/GG/PPI hydrogels showed more sustained release. Cur-β-TCP/GG/PPI hydrogel also produced significantly greater antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli than the HA- and BCP-containing formulations, while no significant differences among the three formulations were observed against Staphylococcus aureus. Overall, the results show that CaP phase composition influenced the physicochemical behavior, curcumin release, and strain-dependent antibacterial response of the injectable GG/PPI hydrogels, supporting their potential as localized drug delivery systems for bone-related applications.

item.title: Photoswitching Quantum Yield of Reversibly Switchable Fluorescent Proteins Depends on Wavelength and Temperature
item.description:
Abstract
Reversibly switchable fluorescent proteins (RSFPs) enable super-resolved bioimaging by leveraging the photoswitching between their On- and Off-forms. The photoswitching quantum yield (ϕ) is the key parameter that characterizes the switching efficiency of RSFPs, yet reported values vary widely. Although the quantum yield of molecular organic photoswitches is known to depend on both temperature and excitation wavelength, these dependencies have often been overlooked in studies of RSFPs. To study the modulation of ϕ, an RSFP designed from enhanced green fluorescent protein (rsEGFP2), as well as two of its variants, was selected. The wild-type rsEGFP2 is a representative RSFP that has been reported multiple times in the literature on nanoscopy and exhibits up to 4-fold variation in the reported values of ϕ. We measured the dependence of ϕ values on temperature (from 10 to 35 °C) and on irradiation wavelength (408 and 480 nm) across variants, reflecting distinct cis–trans excited-state isomerization pathways. These results suggest that temperature and wavelength dependencies are general properties of RSFPs and may offer new insights into their photoswitching mechanisms, enabling the development of novel temperature- and color-modulated imaging strategies.

item.title: Development of Iron-Doped ZnSe Microcrystal-Embedded Tellurite Glasses for Mid-Infrared Emission
item.description:
Abstract
Transition-metal (TM)-doped chalcogenides are promising solid-state materials for mid-infrared (MIR) laser emission. However, incorporating these optical materials into MIR-transparent glass is a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate the successful incorporation of micrometer-sized, iron-doped chalcogenide (Fe:ZnSe) in laboratory-synthesized tellurite glass (TeO2: 60%, Ba(CO3)2: 20%, and ZnO: 20% molar basis), which emits photoluminescence (PL) in the MIR region (3600 to 4200 nm) at different temperatures (7 to 200 K), similar to bulk Fe:ZnSe (3400 to 4500 nm) and Fe:ZnSe in a chalcogenide glass matrix (3520 to 5200 nm). The low glass transition temperature of the tellurite provides the successful incorporation of the microcrystal into the molten matrix and the vitreous nature of the matrix, which opens the possibility of eventual fiberization. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), in situ TEM, and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) together with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis confirm the size, crystallinity, and composition of the Fe:ZnSe incorporated within the tellurite glass. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with EDX established the chemical integrity of the Fe:ZnSe throughout the tellurite glass. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) experiments showed the transmissivity of Fe:ZnSe and Fe:ZnSe-incorporated tellurite glass in the MIR region. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis confirmed the presence of an iron dopant within the tellurite matrix. The XPS spectrum exhibits a broad and weak profile, reflecting the low dopant content and background contributions from the heavy-element host matrix. PL confirmed the emission of Fe:ZnSe and Fe:ZnSe in tellurite glass in the MIR region. Temperature-dependent PL measurements (7 to 200 K) of the Fe:ZnSe-incorporated glass further corroborate the existing literature reports. Ultimately, this work represents a significant step toward developing tunable, crystalline semiconductor optical materials capable of direct MIR laser emission and strengthens the feasibility of fabricating novel fiber laser materials.

item.title: Citric Acid Tunes the Surface Oxygen of Glucose-Derived Carbon Dots for Gram-Selective Bacterial Fluorescence Labeling
item.description:
Abstract
Carbon dots (CDs) are inexpensive, Water-dispersible fluorophores whose photoluminescence and interactions with biological surfaces are largely determined by their surface chemistry, which is most often tuned by doping the carbon core with heteroatoms. In the current study, we show that the surface of nitrogen-free, glucose-derived CDs can instead be engineered using citric acid alone. Four samples (G, GC1/0.1, GC1/1, and GC1/3) were prepared by a single 30 min microwave reaction in water, differing only in the glucose-to-citric-acid ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy showed that increasing the amount of citric acid raised the surface oxygen content from 32.6 to 53.3 at. % and enriched the carbonyl (C = O) and carboxyl (O–C = O) groups, whereas the amorphous carbon core and the particle size (3.5–3.7 nm) remained unchanged. This surface oxidation blue-shifted the excitation-dependent emission from 517 to 445 nm, raised the quantum yield from 13.5 to 16.4%, and made the surface more negatively charged (ζ potential from – 23.3 to – 26.1 mV). When applied to a panel of 12 bacteria, the optimized GC1/3 dots labeled all six Gram-positive species but left all six Gram-negative species unstained; brightfield images confirmed that intact cells were present in the unlabeled fields. Electron microscopy further revealed envelope-bound deposits on Bacillus subtilis only after CD treatment, and a CCK-8 assay defined a usable working concentration at or below 200 ppm. Together, these results establish a dopant-free, surface-oxygen strategy for a rapid (5 min) and reagent-simple fluorescence read-out of Gram type.

item.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of 1,4-Naphthoquinone-1,2,3-triazole Hybrids as Potential Antivenom Agents against Bothrops spp. Snake Venoms
item.description:
Abstract
Snakebite envenomation is a neglected tropical disease associated with substantial morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for complementary approaches to conventional antivenom therapy. Herein, 12 1,4-naphthoquinone-1,2,3-triazole hybrids (6a–l) were investigated for their ability to inhibit toxic activities induced by the venoms of Bothrops jararaca and B. jararacussu. The compounds were obtained through an ultrasound-assisted copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) between 2-(azidomethyl)-3-methylnaphthalene-1,4-dione (4) and terminal alkynes (5), affording the derivatives in 54–92% yields. Their effects on venom proteolytic, coagulant, and phospholipase A2 (PLA2) activities were evaluated after incubation with the venoms for 30 min at 37 °C. In addition, in silico ADME and toxicity analyses were performed to assess their physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties. All compounds complied with Lipinski’s rule of five, although low predicted aqueous solubility was observed for some derivatives and a toxicity alert was identified for 6k. In vitro assays showed that most compounds inhibited venom proteolytic activity by 30–90%, with distinct responses depending on the venom species. Notably, 6i showed no inhibition against B. jararaca venom but reduced proteolytic activity of B. jararacussu by approximately 60%. Compounds 6c, 6g, and 6i also displayed selective inhibition of venom-induced fibrinogen coagulation. Regarding PLA2 activity, 6a completely inhibited the activity of B. jararaca venom, while 6b and 6h produced approximately 92% inhibition; against B. jararacussu, measurable inhibition was observed for 6a, 6e, and 6f. Overall, the results reveal compounds- and venom species-dependent inhibitory profiles and provide biological evidence supporting further investigation of 1,4-naphthoquinone-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as potential scaffolds for complementary approaches to snakebite envenomation.

item.title: A Perchlorate Pentagonal-Bipyramidal Dy(III) Single-Ion Magnet: Structure–Magnetism Correlations and Computational Analysis of Magnetization Relaxation
item.description:
Abstract
First-sphere axiality is a key design principle for high-performance Dy(III) single-ion magnets, but magnetic relaxation can also be influenced by the surrounding solid-state environment. Here, we report a perchlorate member of the phosphine-oxide-supported pentagonal-bipyramidal Dy(III) SIM family, [Dy(H2O)5(Cy3PO)2](ClO4)3·2Cy3PO (1; Cy3PO = tricyclohexylphosphine oxide), together with its magnetically diluted Y(III) analogue. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction shows that 1 retains a highly axial pseudo-D5h DyO7 coordination sphere, comprising two axial Cy3PO oxygen donors and five equatorial water ligands, embedded within a perchlorate/Cy3PO second-sphere hydrogen-bonding network. Magnetic measurements reveal slow relaxation of magnetization, FC/ZFC divergence near 8 K, open low-temperature hysteresis loops with QTM-like features, and an effective Arrhenius barrier of 584 K. The enhanced hysteresis observed for the diluted sample is consistent with suppression of Dy···Dy dipolar-assisted relaxation. ORCA/SINGLE_ANISO calculations give an almost ideal Ising ground Kramers doublet with its easy axis aligned along the Oax–Dy–Oax direction. The second excited Kramers doublet lies at 647.6 K, above but in the same energy region as the experimental barrier, and displays pronounced transverse character. These results show that an almost ideal axial DyO7 first coordination sphere does not by itself determine the excited-state anisotropy or relaxation dynamics in this structural family.

item.title: Predicting Infinite-Dilution Activity Coefficients for Unseen Solutes and Solvents: Accuracy and Uncertainty
item.description:
Abstract
Infinite-dilution activity coefficients (IDACs) provide a thermodynamic basis for comparing solvents, but the reliability of learned predictions depends on the chemistry available during training. We evaluated descriptor models and a Gibbs–Helmholtz graph neural network using 11,832 development observations spanning 541 molecular identities and a reserved literature panel of 2809 binary systems. For ExtraTrees with interaction descriptors (ET-I), mean absolute error in ln γ∞ increased from 0.112 under random splitting to 0.238 for unseen pairs, 0.265 for unseen solutes, and 0.327 for unseen solvents. When both identities were unseen, mean error was 0.673 ± 0.480 across five partitions (median 0.434); only the highest-error partition contained water-solvent test records. The graph model reduced mean error to 0.206 for pair holdout and 0.593 for double holdout, with 70% of its summed double-holdout improvement concentrated in that water-containing partition. Repeated training preserved the lower mean errors relative to ET-I but changed the ordering of models in individual partitions. Sensitivity analyses showed that large replicate disagreements did not account for the water error. Leading physical models were more accurate than ET-I on matched literature systems. Solvent-switch direction agreement increased with predicted contrast magnitude in retrospective comparisons, although candidate ranking uncertainty was not calibrated. Chemical support, partition variability, and contrast-level performance therefore determine how these predictions can inform solvent comparisons beyond familiar systems.

item.title: Metabolic Engineering of Yarrowia lipolytica to Enhance Erythritol Biosynthesis
item.description:
Abstract
Erythritol is a four-carbon polyol found in fruits and fermented foods. As a natural sweetener, it is one of the most promising sugar substitutes in functional foods. Microbial fermentation by the yeast Yarrowia lipolytica offers sustainable, safe, and efficient industrial production of erythritol. In this study, we used a diploid industrial erythritol-producing strain of Y. lipolytica named YP060-3 as the chassis cell. To overcome the incomplete genetic manipulation system and low gene-editing efficiency of YP060-3, we first established an efficient genetic manipulation system for YP060-3 based on CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technology. Systematic optimization of gene editing in YP060-3 was performed across multiple dimensions: increasing sgRNA quantity, optimizing plasmid concentration, and modifying the 5′ GT bases of sgRNAs. This enabled successful knockout of the KU70 gene in YP060-3. Concurrently, fermentation conditions were optimized to determine the optimal concentration of glucose and metal ions for erythritol production in YP060-3. Subsequently, systematic metabolic engineering modifications were conducted in order to improve the production of erythritol. First, the erythritol degradation pathway and competitive metabolic bypass were effectively blocked by knocking out the erythritol dehydrogenase gene (EYD1) and the mannitol synthesis gene (MDH2). Second, based on a multimodular metabolic engineering strategy, overexpression of key genes in each module revealed the hexose transport protein gene (YHT3) and ribose-5-phosphate isomerase gene (RPI) as highly effective for enhancing erythritol titer. Third, rational design and protein engineering of the rate-limiting enzyme erythrose reductase ER25 resulted in the mutant ER25K42R, with significantly enhanced catalytic activity. Fourth, the identified beneficial genes were expressed in a multigene cascade configuration. Finally, the verruconus hemoglobin gene (VHb) was introduced to optimize oxygen utilization efficiency, while the phosphoketolase gene (Bbxfpk) from Bifidobacterium breve was integrated to redirect carbon flux. The resulting YP-32 strain achieved 278 g/L of erythritol after 104 h of fermentation, with a yield of 0.88 g/g and productivity of 2.67 g/L/h, representing the highest titer reported so far at the 5-L fermenter scale. Furthermore, phenotypic comparison results show that knockout of the KU70 gene does not induce adverse phenotypes. The metabolic engineering strategy in this study can alter the micromorphology of the high-yield strain and optimize its growth characteristics, providing support for high erythritol production.

item.title: Femtosecond Transient Response of Quantum-Interference-Governed Benzene Molecular Junctions
item.description:
Abstract
We study the femtosecond response of para- and meta-connected benzene junctions to a voltage pulse with a time-dependent wave function method in the wide-band limit, in which the bias is applied to the electrodes, and the electronic Hamiltonian remains Hermitian. The calculations reproduce the Landauer current exactly in the steady state (median ratio 0.999 over 41 runs). The para junction (G = 8.5 × 10–3G0 for Γ = 0.5 eV) rises to its plateau in τset ≈3.3 fs. The meta junction, whose steady-state current vanishes because of destructive quantum interference (DQI) at the Fermi level, nevertheless carries switching transients of ∼ 16 nA at 10 mV, comparable to those of the para isomer. Both transients ring at ℏω ≃ 2.7 eV, the energy of the molecular resonances relative to EF. The ringing lasts longer in the meta junction because both members of the degenerate π pair couple to the leads and form a long-lived combination (ℏ/|Im λ| = 15.8 fs), whereas in the para junction one member is a decoupled dark state. An amino or hydroxyl group on C4 lifts the DQI node (T(EF) = 1.6 × 10–4 and 3.1 × 10–5) and adds spectral lines, but it changes the damping time only weakly. All femtosecond time scales scale with the electrode coupling Γ, are insensitive to the pulse shape, and are robust against the substituent parameters, the level alignment, and a self-consistent Hartree treatment.

item.title: Mixture-of-Prompts for Parameter-Efficient ADMET Prediction
item.description:
Abstract
Accurate prediction of absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties is central to modern drug discovery, yet building separate, fully fine-tuned models for each end point is computationally costly and difficult to scale across many heterogeneous tasks. At the same time, recent molecular foundation models provide rich, transferable representations that invite more parameter-efficient adaptation strategies. In this work, we propose a Mixture-of-Prompts (MoP) framework for parameter-efficient single-task ADMET prediction on top of a frozen molecular encoder. For each end point, we keep the backbone fixed and introduce a small set of learnable prompt “experts” together with a lightweight gating network. Given the encoder representation of a molecule, the gate produces a dense mixture over the experts, whose pooled prompt embedding is concatenated with the frozen molecular embedding and fed into a shallow prediction head. This design allows each end point to express task-specific behavior through a compact prompt expert pool, while updating only a small fraction of the total parameters. We instantiate MoP on the standardized PharmaBench ADMET benchmark, training a separate MoP-adapted model for each of the 11 end points under both random and scaffold splits, and further evaluate it on external OpenADMET/ExpansionRx end points. Experiments show that MoP matches or improves upon strong baselines based on head-only adaptation, LoRA, and prefix tuning on many end points, with robust performance under scaffold-split evaluation and informative behavior under external distribution shift. These results suggest that modeling mixtures of prompt experts on top of frozen molecular foundation models provides a flexible and scalable route toward foundation-model-based ADMET modeling.

item.title: Pre-Training Synthetic Accessibility Filtering in PyRMD under Transferred Percentile Cutoffs across 95 Target Data Sets
item.description:
Abstract
Synthetic accessibility filtering before cross-validation changes both the compounds available for learning and those used to evaluate ligand-based virtual screening models. We assessed SAscore filtering in PyRMD using SA-Filter Impact Benchmarking (SA-FIB), with 95 unfiltered target data sets and 438 filtered conditions across five thresholds. Historical residual-distance percentile cutoffs were transferred, while absolute epsilon values were estimated within each training subset. Mean paired F1 differences were −0.1078, −0.0361, −0.0147, −0.0074, and −0.0011 at SA ≤ 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, and 5.0, respectively, relative to the corresponding eligible-cohort baselines. At SA ≤ 5.0, the F1 difference was not significant after Bonferroni correction, while ROC-AUC and PRC-AUC increased by 0.005085 and 0.003060. Combining duplicated processed pools into 92 units retained significance for ROC-AUC but not PRC-AUC. Reoptimizing percentile cutoffs within inner folds for the 92 eligible SA ≤ 3.5 data sets changed mean outer-fold F1 by +0.000294, with 30 improvements, 22 ties, and 40 decreases. Responses varied by target and metric. Historical parameter selection, reused outer folds, and differences between baseline and filtered evaluation populations limit interpretation to sensitivity within this PyRMD protocol. These findings support target-specific validation of synthetic accessibility filters.

item.title: Study on an Oxygen Candle-Driven Integrated Expansion Capsule-Mucus Sealing and Pressure Measurement Device for Coal-Seam Gas
item.description:
Abstract
Building on the working principles of conventional borehole sealing and gas pressure measurement technologies for coal mines, this study designs a novel capsule-viscose self-pressurizing sealing and pressure measurement device, which consists of a pressure booster, expansion capsules, a mucus storage unit, and an automatic pressure monitoring module. Solid chlorate-based oxygen candles are adopted as the built-in chemical pressure source, and systematic laboratory tests are carried out to optimize the oxygen-candle formulation. Coupled with a programmable logic controller system, borehole sealing and pressure measurement experiments as well as performance verification tests are implemented. The experimental results reveal that the optimal mass ratio of chlorate, exothermic material, catalyst, and binder for the oxygen candle is 88:6:5:1; this formulation achieves stable decomposition, a moderate reaction temperature, and effective pressure rise, which qualifies it as a reliable pressure source for borehole sealing. On the basis of simulated borehole tests, a quantitative correlation among oxygen candle mass, reaction chamber volume, and system sealing pressure is established. Under standard working conditions of conventional borehole sealers, the required oxygen candle mass is 445 g for the capsule zone and 297 g for the mucus zone, and the developed device achieves a maximum sealing capacity of 0.932 MPa for gas containment. The proposed integrated apparatus overcomes the drawbacks of traditional sealing technologies, including complicated field deployment and poor reliability under complex underground geological conditions. This work provides an efficient technical approach for in situ and accurate measurement of coal-seam gas pressure.

item.title: Niacinamide–Ceramide Conjugate: In Vitro Bioactivities and 28-Day Clinical Evidence for Multitarget Skincare
item.description:
Abstract
Niacinamide (NAM) and ceramides are well-established skincare ingredients with distinct yet complementary biological mechanisms. Nevertheless, simple physical blending of these two actives presents practical limitations for topical application. To address this, the present study evaluated SuperCera N-Nicotinamide(P) (NAM-Cer), a niacinamide–ceramide covalent conjugate conceived to integrate bioactivities derived from each parent moiety within a single molecular framework. Employing an integrated workflow combining in vitro cellular assays and a 28-day randomized clinical trial, we identified multiple cellular-level bioactivities of NAM-Cer, including elastase inhibition, upregulation of type I collagen (COL1A1) and aquaporin-3 (AQP3), suppression of melanogenesis and tyrosinase activity, and downregulation of matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1). Clinical evaluation revealed significant, concentration-dependent improvements in skin hydration, elasticity, firmness, brightness, and antiwrinkle efficacy, along with favorable cutaneous tolerability. In summary, NAM-Cer is a safe, multitarget skincare candidate that elicits diverse skin-beneficial bioactivities in vitro and drives concentration-dependent cutaneous improvements in short-term human topical use.

item.title: Deep Hydrocarbon Sources, Charging History, and Late-Stage Tectonic Modification in the Qimeigan Area, Southwestern Tarim Basin
item.description:
Abstract
The Qimeigan area in the southwestern Tarim Basin contains multiple potential source intervals and records multistage hydrocarbon charging followed by tectonic modification. This study integrates biomarker data from five Carboniferous source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1 and two from Well Qiqian-2), 11 Qipan Formation source-rock samples (three from Well Shatan-1, three from Well Qiqian-1, and five from Well Kuntan-1), and three Kangkelin Formation reservoir-rock extracts from Well Shatan-1. Natural-gas geochemical data include seven gas samples from Wells Shatan-1 and Kuntan-1, among which four samples (three from Well Shatan-1 and one from Well Kuntan-1) were analyzed for carbon isotopes, together with fluid-inclusion petrography and microthermometry and burial–thermal history. The reservoir liquid hydrocarbons show a stronger geochemical affinity with the Carboniferous source rocks, although a Qipan Formation contribution cannot be excluded. Natural gas has dryness coefficients of 0.985–0.999 and isotopic characteristics of high- to overmature thermogenic dry gas. The Carboniferous is interpreted as the most likely gas-supplying interval based on its deep burial, advanced thermal evolution, and regional petroleum-system framework, although contributions from other mature source intervals cannot be excluded. Petrographic relationships distinguish earlier and later fluid assemblages, with associated aqueous inclusions defining broad Th populations at 120–125 °C and 140–145 °C. Projection onto the burial–thermal history yields approximate fluid-activity windows of 20–14 Ma and 9–4 Ma. The earlier stage is oil-related, whereas the later stage records gas-dominated overprinting of earlier liquid hydrocarbons. Late tectonic activity mainly controlled remigration, redistribution, and differential preservation rather than a third independent charging event. The present reservoir state therefore reflects the coupling of hydrocarbon supply, fluid-phase evolution, fault effectiveness, and late-stage preservation.

item.title: Enhanced Stabilization of Steel Slag for Road Aggregate via Dual-Functional-Group Chelation of Poly(acrylic acid- co -vinylphosphonic acid)
item.description:
Abstract
The volume expansion induced by residual free calcium oxide (f-CaO) in steel slag remains the primary limitation to its widespread application in pavement engineering. To address this issue, a novel polymer modifier (PAV) was synthesized via the aqueous radical polymerization of acrylic acid (AA) and vinylphosphonic acid (VPA). The effects of monomer ratios on the chemical structure, thermal stability, and Ca2+ chelation performance of PAV were systematically investigated using GPC, FTIR, SEM-EDS, and TGA. The modification mechanism of PAV on steel slag was revealed through systematic characterization and performance tests. Furthermore, the key process parameters for PAV-modified steel slag were optimized, and the volume stability and mechanical properties of the modified steel slag were comprehensively evaluated. The results indicated that the synthesized PAV exhibited a uniform molecular weight distribution and excellent thermal stability. Through the chelation effect of carboxyl and phosphonic acid groups, PAV can efficiently eliminate f-CaO in steel slag. When the mass ratio of AA to VPA is 8.5:1.5, PAV exhibits the optimal Ca2+ chelation performance, with a chelation capacity reaching 376 mg/g. The optimal modification concentration of PAV was determined to be 1.0 wt %. Under this condition, the f-CaO content of the modified steel slag was reduced to 0.54%, with a 10-day water immersion expansion rate of merely 0.46%, which was far below the standard limit. Meanwhile, the PAV modification did not damage the inorganic crystalline skeleton of the steel slag. Instead, it reduced its water absorption, aggregate crushing value, and Los Angeles abrasion value, thereby further optimizing its mechanical properties.

item.title: Study on Ionic Liquid-Modified ZIF-8 Composite Materials and Their CO 2 Adsorption Performance
item.description:
Abstract
Driven by the dual carbon goals, developing novel carbon capture technologies is crucial. Adsorption methods have become a research focus due to their simplicity in operation, wide range of adsorbent options, and low cost. To enhance the CO2 adsorption performance of ZIF-8, this study employed amino acid–based ionic liquids as modifiers ([emim]Gly and N2222Gly) to prepare ZIF-IL composite materials via the impregnation method. The structural characteristics of the composite materials were characterized, and their CO2 adsorption performances were evaluated. Results indicated that the ILs were successfully loaded onto the pores and surface of ZIF-8 through hydrogen bonding and coordination interactions. ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-N2222Gly retained intact crystalline structures and polyhedral morphologies, but the specific surface area and pore volume decreased, indicating that the incorporation of ILs occupied part of the pores of ZIF-8. CO2 adsorption tests revealed that the adsorption capacities of ZIF-8, ZIF-[emim]Gly, and ZIF-N2222Gly were 1.27, 0.83, and 0.74 mmol·g–1, respectively, under the conditions of 700 mmHg and 298 K. Although ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-8-N2222Gly provided additional active sites for CO2 adsorption via acid–base synergistic effects, they could not compensate for the loss of pore structure of ZIF-8. However, compared with ZIF-8, the CO2/N2 selectivity of ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-N2222Gly was significantly improved. The isosteric heats of ZIF-8, ZIF-[emim]Gly, and ZIF-8-N2222Gly were 8.3–11.7, 10.7–36.7, and 9.1–25.7 kJ·mol–1, respectively. The introduction of ILs significantly enhanced the adsorption forces for CO2, providing experimental and theoretical foundations for the development of high-performance CO2 adsorption materials.

item.title: Synthesis and SERS Evaluation of Cu/Cu 2 O Microtubes
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, Cu/Cu2O microtubes were fabricated by electroless deposition on polymer templates and evaluated as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The structural, morphological, and optical properties of the substrate were characterized by XRD, SEM/EDS, XPS, and UV–vis spectroscopy. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of face-centered cubic copper (90.1%) with a minor Cu2O phase (9.9%), while XPS showed that the surface was dominated by Cu0/Cu+ species with a minor contribution from Cu2+ species. UV–vis absorption spectroscopy revealed a broad absorption band in the 400–600 nm range. Additional electromagnetic modeling was used to evaluate the optical and near-field response of the Cu structures. The SERS performance of the substrate was evaluated using four probe analytes: methylene blue, methyl violet, eosin yellow, and potassium chromate. Analytical enhancement factors ranging from 0.2 × 103 to 0.8 × 104 were obtained, depending on the analyte.

item.title: Ligand-Free Ni 2+ Immobilization on Poly(acrylic acid)-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles for His-Tagged Protein Purification
item.description:
Abstract
The development of simplified, ligand-free magnetic affinity platforms holds promise for advancing future recombinant protein purification technologies. Purification of His6-tagged proteins, essential in biotechnology and biopharmaceutical production, is commonly achieved via immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (IMAC). However, magnetic IMAC systems commonly require additional chelating ligands for Ni2+ immobilization, increasing surface functionalization complexity. Developing a ligand-free magnetic platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization could therefore simplify this purification process. Poly(acrylic acid) (PAA)-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were developed as a simple ligand-free platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization and selective purification of His6-tagged proteins, exploiting the intrinsic metal-coordination capability of surface carboxylate groups. MNPs were synthesized by chemical coprecipitation and subsequently coated with PAA of two molecular weights (2 and 100 kDa) to systematically investigate the influence of polymer chain length on physicochemical properties, Ni2+ immobilization efficiency, and bioseparation performance. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy revealed a decrease in the free carboxylic acid stretching band and a concurrent increase in the carboxylate coordination band upon Ni2+ immobilization, supporting the involvement of PAA carboxylate groups in Ni2+ immobilization, consistent with a proposed carboxylate–metal interaction at the nanoparticle surface. Complementarily, zeta potential analysis demonstrated progressive surface charge evolution from bare MNPs to PAA-coated and Ni2+-loaded states, consistent with PAA adsorption and subsequent Ni2+ immobilization. The purification performance of both systems was then evaluated using His6-tagged Plasmodium falciparum serine hydroxymethyltransferase (His6-tagged PfSHMT) as a model protein. Despite both systems achieving near-complete adsorption, MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ exhibited significantly higher desorption efficiency (63.5 ± 6.7%) than MNPs–PAA(100 kDa)–Ni2+ (37.8 ± 6.1%), demonstrating different protein recovery between the two PAA formulations investigated. The optimized MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ system achieved rapid protein capture within 15 min and selective purification over nontagged proteins (BSA and lysozyme). Further application to crude E. coli cell lysate demonstrated enrichment of His6-tagged PfSHMT with retained enzymatic activity and a 326-fold purification. These findings establish PAA-functionalized MNPs as a simple and effective ligand-free nanoplatform for selective affinity-based bioseparation of His6-tagged proteins.

item.title: Flexible Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Photodetector Based on a Freestanding β-Ga 2 O 3 /BTO Semiconductor/Ferroelectric Heterostructure
item.description:
Abstract
Excessive ultraviolet (UV) exposure causes cumulative harm to human health, creating a growing demand for wearable devices that enable real-time UV monitoring. Among various UV-sensitive materials, β-Ga2O3 is particularly attractive because of its wide bandgap, intrinsic solar-blind response, high sensitivity, and excellent stability. However, its intrinsic brittleness and the high temperatures required for growth on rigid substrates limit its use in flexible electronics. Here, we report a flexible solar-blind Ga2O3 photodetector based on a freestanding ferroelectric BaTiO3 (BTO)/Ga2O3 heterostructure fabricated using a nondestructive, water-soluble transfer strategy. Spontaneous polarization in the BTO layer generates a built-in electric field that promotes the separation of photogenerated carriers. In addition, polarization rotation and domain evolution provide ferroelastic strain accommodation, enabling effective stress relaxation and improving the mechanical stability of the flexible device. The device retained more than 90% of its initial photocurrent after 1000 bending cycles at a bending radius of 7.5 mm. It was further integrated into wearable devices, including a wristband, smart sunglasses, and a ring, demonstrating its mechanical conformability and integration capability on wearable platforms. This work offers an effective strategy for integrating brittle wide-bandgap semiconductors into flexible devices and advances wearable solar-blind UV sensing technologies.

item.title: Dual-Functional Halloysite Nanotube-Derived Cigarette Capsules for Hazard Reduction and Mold Prevention
item.description:
Abstract
Currently, cigarette-filter modification has predominantly targeted reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging; however, beyond ROS, cigarette smoke contains other hazardous agents such as carbon monoxide (CO), tar, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the reduction of which remains largely neglected in current strategies. Herein, we report a novel cigarette-filter capsule, termed Cit-sHNT@Capsule, fabricated by loading the natural flavor citral (Cit) into sulfuric acid-etched halloysite nanotubes and further encapsulating the hybrid within alginate-based hydrogel beads. Incorporating Cit-sHNT@Capsule into cigarette filters moderately reduced CO and tar yields by 9.74% and 13.4%, respectively, while the •OH and •O2– probe assays indicated reductions of approximately 50% and 60%, and fluorescence-based calibration yielded an apparent 57.0% reduction in the PAH-associated measurement, without compromising the moisture and nicotine content during combustion. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated limited mass loss over 70–80 °C, and the capsules retained their structural integrity under the heating conditions, providing preliminary support for their incorporation into cigarette filters. Furthermore, the outstanding antifungal activity of Cit-sHNT@Capsule against Aspergillus niger (nearly 100% inhibition within 45 days) underscored the potential to extend tobacco storage duration and reduce fungal contamination. Collectively, this work highlights the potential of Cit-sHNT@Capsule as a dual-functional additive for cigarette filters, enabling simultaneous hazard reduction and mold prevention.

item.title: Influence of a Single Nitrogen Atom on the π–π Stacking Interaction in Coronene Dimers: An EDA, QTAIM, and NCI Computational Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Intermolecular aromatic interactions, also known as π–π stacking, are of great importance in chemical and biological materials science. This field of study has remained important for at least three decades and spans a broad multidisciplinary range. Doping aromatic systems with heteroatoms, such as nitrogen, can influence these interactions and significantly alter their properties. Still, the exact cause of the altered π–π interactions in aromatic aggregates from heteroatom doping remains debated. In this work, we evaluate changes in the electronic and structural properties of coronene dimers upon introducing a single nitrogen heteroatom. Calculations use CAM–B3LYP–D3/6–311G(d,p) level of theory, along with EDA, QTAIM, and NCI analyses. Our results show that nitrogen subtly enhances π–π interactions between coronene monomers. The strength of these interactions varies with the substitution site. Aggregation becomes stronger with increased N–N distance when pyridinic–N is the substituent, if the same arrangement is considered (twisted or parallel–displaced). When graphitic–N is substituted at an intermediary position, the degree of slipping between monomers mainly governs aggregation, regardless of the arrangement. In the central ring, graphitic–N promotes the formation of a covalent C–C bond between the monomers, promoting a 10 kcal mol–1 increase in interaction energy. The results indicate that dispersive forces, such as pancake bond, remain the primary driver of aggregation, with nitrogen only slightly altering the electronic charge distribution. Energy decomposition analysis indicates that dispersion remains the dominant stabilizing contribution, while the type and position of the nitrogen atom locally modulate the electronic environment and promote distinct geometrical reorganizations of the π–π interface, thereby affecting the interaction strength and preferred stacking arrangements.

item.title: Scientific Insights into the Illegible and Discolored Red and Green Inks in Arabic Papyrus Protocols
item.description:
Abstract
Papyrus protocols are texts written on the outermost sheet of a papyrus roll, providing information relevant to its manufacture in a state-controlled facility. Arabic papyrus protocols constitute a key corpus of manuscripts that feature colored inks in early Islamic Egypt, with red and green inks used alongside iron-gall ink for writing the text. To expand our limited knowledge of the early Islamic color palette, 14 Arabic papyrus protocols preserved at the Austrian National Library in Vienna were subjected to non-destructive analysis combining scanning XRF spectroscopy with vibrational spectroscopies. Visual examination indicated that both colored inks exhibited signs of degradation. The red ink, in particular, appeared to be significantly discolored, rendering sections of the text illegible. The green ink was identified as a copper-based green, with moolooite (CuC2O4·nH2O) as the primary component. The red ink was identified as red lead (Pb3O4). Chlorine was also detected alongside lead in the red ink in 12 cases; its presence could be attributed to both intrinsic (e.g., ink formulation) and extrinsic (e.g., migration from a chlorine-rich environment) factors. The results from semi-quantitative analysis suggested that the Pb3O4 content in the red ink, though low, was sufficient to create a clear contrast on a fresh papyrus sheet. Based on these results, we tentatively propose that the observed discoloration was likely caused by a combination of factors, including pigment and support degradation. Finally, the results allowed us to improve the legibility of the faded sections of the text and reconstruct their original layout.

item.title: Thermally Altered Pore-Fracture Structures and Water Seepage Behaviors in Shale Characterized by LF-NMR Measurements and Numerical Simulations
item.description:
Abstract
Shale is a tight medium with low porosity and permeability, and fluid seepage takes place across interconnected pores and fractures. Thermal stimulation triggers shale cracking, alters pore-fracture geometry, fluid properties, and seepage rules, so as to boost shale gas output. Most existing studies on shale fluid flow under temperature conditions focus solely on either freeze damage at low temperatures or thermal damage at high temperatures. They lack comprehensive characterization over a wide temperature range spanning from extremely low to moderate-to-high temperatures. Furthermore, most studies regard experimental testing and numerical simulation as separate efforts. Few investigations combine low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) microporosity measurements and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)-reconstructed thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) multiphysics simulations for comparative validation. Studying fluid flow in shale pore-fracture networks under variable temperatures is practically important for efficient shale gas exploitation. In this work, shale outcrops from Jiujiang were tested via LF-NMR and COMSOL THM simulations to clarify pore-fracture evolution, fluid distribution, and water seepage features under different thermal conditions. T2 spectra show low-temperature freezing forms ice plugs inside pores, cutting pore connectivity, and movable fluid volume. High temperatures weaken mineral adsorption to release bound water; thermal expansion and cracking connect tiny pores to form unobstructed flow channels. Real pore-fracture models reconstructed from SEM images were adopted for coupled simulations. Simulation outcomes indicate that frost heave squeezes pore throats at low temperatures, raising flow resistance and lowering permeability. Rising temperature reduces water viscosity and generates thermal fractures, greatly improving seepage capacity. Consistent trends between tests and simulations verify the model reliability. Temperature controls shale seepage via two paths: changing fluid physical properties and reconstructing pore-fracture systems. Ice blockage restrains water migration under cold conditions, whereas fluid activation and thermal fractures enhance seepage at high temperatures. This study offers theoretical support for reservoir stimulation and underground high-temperature formation safety assessment.
